a6.speaker: Hounkponou K. Saïd, Director of Water (Bénin)
a6.name: Hounkponou K. Saïd
a6.title: Director of Water (Bénin)
a6.speech: IWRM promotes the coordinated development of water, land, and related resources for equitable economic and social well-being, while ensuring the sustainability of ecosystems.

a119.speaker: Melvin Foote, President and Founder of the “Constituency of Africa”, Washington, D.C.
a119.name: Melvin Foote
a119.title: President and Founder of the “Constituency of Africa”, Washington, D.C.
a119.speech: Is urging the Liberian Government to strengthen its relationships with regional and continental organizations; said the current freeze on aid, through USAID, must be seen as a wakeup call for African leaders to work together to reduce the impact such a decision may have on the continent ; “The ongoing freeze on aid across the world by the United States government is having an unprecedented humanitarian impact on millions.” ; stated that a country like Liberia stands a chance of weaving out the opportunities for strong partnerships with counterparts on the continent.

a119.speaker: Melvin Foote, President and Founder of the “Constituency of Africa”, Washington, D.C.
a119.name: Melvin Foote
a119.title: President and Founder of the “Constituency of Africa”, Washington, D.C.
a119.speech: Lauded President Joseph Boakai for efforts aimed at improving governance in Liberia.

a138.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a138.name: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a138.speech: On Friday urged African health authorities to intensify COVID-19 prevention measures amid the emergence of a new variant: “National health authorities across the continent should reinforce public health and social measures and accelerate immunization of their populations, prioritizing high risk groups, ahead of upcoming new waves of COVID-19 infections,” the agency said in a statement.

a138.speaker: National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD), South Africa
a138.name: National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD)
a138.title: South Africa
a138.speech: Announced the detection of a new variant, B.1.1.529, of the SARS-COV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19 pandemic.

a138.speaker: World Health Organization
a138.name: World Health Organization
a138.speech: On Friday classified the new variant as a “Variant of Concern.”

a138.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a138.name: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a138.speech: Called on African countries to expedite COVID-19 vaccination drive to halt the spread of the virus, saying “vaccines remain a key tool to prevent severe cases and deaths from COVID-19 infection” ; underscored the need to reinforce timely genomic surveillance through coordination with national and regional pathogen genomics laboratories.

a138.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a138.name: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a138.speech: According to the agency, as of Saturday the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases in Africa has reached 8,616,912 with 222,301 deaths and 8,064,499 recoveries.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Adopted a draft law authorising the President of the Republic to ratify the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in Africa, stating that ratification will reaffirm the country's constitutional commitment to promote and protect all categories of human rights and consolidate the rights of persons with disabilities throughout the national territory.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Adopted an ordinance specifying that the local electorate concerned by the sponsorship requirement for presidential candidates is that of the thirty-one (31) regions and the two (02) autonomous Districts of Abidjan and Yamoussoukro, a measure that aims to avoid an increase in the number of administrative constituencies where sponsorships would be required.

a198.speaker: Independent Electoral Commission (CEI) of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.name: Independent Electoral Commission (CEI) of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.speech: Proposed the ordinance specifying the local electorate concerned by presidential candidate sponsorship.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Adopted a decree organising the continuing training of civil servants and State agents, which extends the maximum duration of long-term continuing training and of professional training leave to six years and institutes the validation of acquired experience.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Adopted decrees ratifying two military cooperation agreements with Türkiye, stating they will allow the armed forces to benefit from Türkiye's experience in defence industry, military medicine and military information electronic systems and will raise interoperability in multinational exercises focused on counter-terrorism, maritime piracy and peacekeeping.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Adopted decrees ratifying an Instalment Sale Framework Agreement and a Loan Agreement with the Islamic Development Bank for the cassava value chain development project, whose objective is to improve the resilience of the food production system and strengthen food and nutritional security.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Gave its agreement for the appointment of Mr Mirmohammad Meigoni Seyed Gholamreza as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Côte d'Ivoire.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Adopted a communication on Côte d'Ivoire's participation in the IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings, noting that the meetings were marked by uncertainties in the global economy linked to escalating customs duties and worsening trade tensions, with global growth projected at 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 2026, down from previous projections.

a198.speaker: IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings (proceedings)
a198.name: IMF and World Bank Spring Meetings (proceedings)
a198.speech: The proceedings recommended caution in the conduct of economic policies and the strengthening of international cooperation, with a view to reducing trade tensions.

a198.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a198.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a198.speech: Welcomed the performance recorded in the ongoing implementation of the Economic and Financial Programme signed with Côte d'Ivoire, as well as the success of the eurobond issue in CFA francs.

a198.speaker: Technical and financial partners met by the Ivorian delegation
a198.name: Technical and financial partners met by the Ivorian delegation
a198.speech: Greatly appreciated the progress made in the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism, as well as the success recorded in debt management operations, and reaffirmed their commitment to continue and intensify their cooperation with Côte d'Ivoire.

a198.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (communiqué)
a198.speech: Instructed the Keeper of the Seals, Minister of Justice and Human Rights, and all Ministers concerned to take appropriate steps to support the candidacy of Bakary Sidiki Diaby for renewal of his mandate on the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.

a198.speaker: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.name: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.speech: On the occasion of the 2025 Labour Day celebration, expressed his deep gratitude to the valiant Ivorian population and to all workers, whose self-sacrifice and labour sustain the growth and resilience of the national economy, and recalled the significant gains granted to workers in the public and private sectors since 2013, amounting cumulatively to more than 3,700 billion CFA francs ; Regarding the new demands formulated by the Trade Union Centres, asked the trade unionists to be patient and to trust the Government so that all demands are dealt with through procedures centred on social dialogue, so as to preserve the major balances of the country's development momentum.

a198.speaker: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.name: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.speech: Announced an exceptional derogatory measure decided by the President of the Republic, allowing the opening of access rights to the CMU (Universal Health Coverage) for insured persons in the informal sector from 2 May until 31 August 2025, under which approximately thirteen million first-time insured persons will benefit without having contributed beforehand, paying only the 30% co-payment, with care completely free in rural health centres, at an estimated cost of 8.4 billion CFA francs.

a198.speaker: Vice-President of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.name: Vice-President of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire
a198.speech: Reported to the Council on the inauguration ceremony of the elected President of the Gabonese Republic, His Excellency Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguéma, and on the audience granted to him by the Gabonese President, which focused essentially on strengthening cooperation between the two countries.

a198.speaker: Amadou Coulibaly, Minister of Communication, Government Spokesperson (Côte d'Ivoire)
a198.name: Amadou Coulibaly
a198.title: Minister of Communication, Government Spokesperson (Côte d'Ivoire)
a198.speech: Issued the communiqué of the Council of Ministers of Wednesday 7 May 2025, announcing that the next Council of Ministers will be held on 22 May 2025 in Abidjan.

a441.speaker: Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO)
a441.name: Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO)
a441.speech: Quashed claims that it has halted investigations into the M200 million for the construction of the Lesotho Standards Institute funded by the African Development Bank (AfDB).

a441.speaker: Ministry of Trade (Lesotho)
a441.name: Ministry of Trade (Lesotho)
a441.speech: Informed Public Eye last month that the deal for LSI, located at Ha Tikoe on the outskirts of Maseru, was above board and that DCEO had cleared them to go ahead with the facility.

a441.speaker: 'Matlhokomelo Senoko, DCEO spokesperson
a441.name: 'Matlhokomelo Senoko
a441.title: DCEO spokesperson
a441.speech: Was emphatic that investigations were proceeding: "I asked the investigator conducting the matter and I was informed that as far he knows he's continuing with the probe. The investigator was told by the Ministry's Procurement Director, Seriti Khabisi about the alleged letter clearing the department" ; maintained that the new anti-graft head, Director General Advocate Brigadier Mantso Sello, is yet to appraise himself with the contents of the said case: "We are currently under a new management, this case (LSI [mis] procurement) is identified for investigations."

a441.speaker: Seriti Khabisi, Procurement Director, Ministry of Trade
a441.name: Seriti Khabisi
a441.title: Procurement Director, Ministry of Trade
a441.speech: Confirmed to this paper that indeed she was on suspension but has since launched a case before the courts.

a441.speaker: Palesa Matobako, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Trade
a441.name: Palesa Matobako
a441.title: Principal Secretary, Ministry of Trade
a441.speech: Said the deal was above-board: "The tender was even investigated by DCEO (Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences) which indicated that there was no foul-play in the awarding of the tender" ; confirmed that Khabisi asked the anti-corruption agency to investigate the tender which "was cleared as legal procedures were followed...she (Khabisi) has an axe to grind" ; "She has been suspended for buying phones and placing adverts in newspapers without following proper procedures not what is being peddled."

a441.speaker: Palesa Matobako, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Trade
a441.name: Palesa Matobako
a441.title: Principal Secretary, Ministry of Trade
a441.speech: Has since indicated that she will never give an interview to this paper.

a441.speaker: Palesa Matobako, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Trade
a441.name: Palesa Matobako
a441.title: Principal Secretary, Ministry of Trade
a441.speech: On the LPMS building where LSI equipment is stored: said the Ministry of Trade was denied access to their equipment by Yan "John" Xie on account that the government owes him; that before Parliament's Economic Cluster they went for inspection with Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) and marketing department staff and met John, who indicated he has a signed sub-lease for the building; that there is a joint venture agreement with Africomforter under which the ministry bought duvet-cover manufacturing machines placed in the LPMS building. "John said he was not going to grant us permission to the building because the government owes him, although he did not disclose the amount" ; "After that incident, we concluded with RSL to open a case in court because what we need is our property and a month after, we requested to have access to at least one machine to continue work and we were granted only that one machine." ; highlighted that to date, they still have not been assisted.

a441.speaker: Source privy to the matter (anonymous)
a441.name: Source privy to the matter (anonymous)
a441.speech: "The AfDB made it clear that there is no way that they can support either the construction or purchase of equipment to be installed whilst commencement of the project is surrounded by so many dubious issues and with relevant ministries failing to provide required answers."

a441.speaker: Neo Matjato Moteane, Minister of Public Works and Transport
a441.name: Neo Matjato Moteane
a441.title: Minister of Public Works and Transport
a441.speech: Revealed last month that Trade has not given his ministry official documents relating to the construction of LSI, informing Public Eye that as principal agents, standard practice documents related to the edifice have not reached his office: "We have not seen documents of the building although we are empowered to as a way of supervising such projects; trade has not yet opened doors for us. We need a letter that indicates that X Company has been awarded a contract, but we have not received such documentation" ; highlighted that since the LSI building has been on and off, it makes it difficult for him to track its progress.

a441.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Minister of Trade
a441.name: Mokhethi Shelile
a441.title: Minister of Trade
a441.speech: Explicitly said, "An EIA is not a requirement," before dropping the phone and informing the reporters to speak to Principal Secretary Palesa Matobako.

a441.speaker: Building Control Act, 1995 (Lesotho)
a441.name: Building Control Act
a441.title: 1995 (Lesotho)
a441.speech: Section 18 (1) read with (2): "(1) No person shall, without the prior approval in writing of the building authority in question, commence any building; (2) A person who contravenes or fails to comply with subsection (1) commits an offense and is liable on conviction to the penalties prescribed in the regulations." ; section 18 subsection (5) stipulates that "the Ministry of Works shall, in respect of all government buildings, submit all plans, specifications, documents, or information as may be required under this Act to the building authority in whose jurisdiction building operations will be carried out."

a441.speaker: E-Regulations website
a441.name: E-Regulations website
a441.speech: Lists twenty-four steps required before starting any construction work for big projects, of which the Land Administration Authority (LAA), Maseru City Council (MCC), Water Sewage Company (WASCO), Lesotho Electricity (LEC), Maseru Fire Brigade, and Roads Directorate are stakeholders.

a441.speaker: Dr Retselisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance (2025/2026 budget speech)
a441.name: Dr Retselisitsoe Matlanyane
a441.title: Minister of Finance (2025/2026 budget speech)
a441.speech: Identified LSI construction during her budget speech, noting that it is meant "to improve market access, the Lesotho Standards Institution (LSI) will be operationalized to handle standards development, testing, and certification. Construction of LSI facilities will begin in the upcoming financial year."

a441.speaker: Yan "John" Xie (as reported by the Principal Secretary)
a441.name: Yan "John" Xie (as reported by the Principal Secretary)
a441.speech: Indicated that he has a signed sub-lease for the LPMS building and said he was not going to grant the ministry permission to the building because the government owes him, although he did not disclose the amount.

a513.speaker: President of the FSSP (Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland), Mrs Brah Reki Hassane Djermakoye
a513.name: President of the FSSP (Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland)
a513.title: Mrs Brah Reki Hassane Djermakoye
a513.speech: "For the National Council for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (CNSP), the resources mobilised must constitute a school and a tool in the exercise of good governance, a model of popular participation in the conquest of food and economic sovereignty. In short, to make the FSSP a financial instrument for Nigeriens and by Nigeriens," declared the president of the FSSP.

a513.speaker: FSSP management committee (weekly bulletin / communications)
a513.name: FSSP management committee (weekly bulletin / communications)
a513.speech: For transparency in the receipt of contributions and to inform the public, the fund's committee communicates through its pages and in the media, with the release of its weekly bulletin recapitulating the voluntary contributions received from the population, public or private companies and any other economic operator, as well as NGOs, associations, development projects and programmes, and also on the levies, for a total of more than 13 billion CFA francs.

a639.speaker: Charge sheet in the treason case (court document)
a639.name: Charge sheet in the treason case (court document)
a639.speech: The words alleged to constitute the offence of treason read: “When they say this position amounts to rebellion, it is true..., because we say we will block the election, we will incite rebellion, that is the way to obtain change..., so we are going to make it stink..., above all we are really going to disrupt this election..., we are going to make it stink very badly...”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked the witness: “Tell the judges, is content that is seditious to the public a treason offence or not a treason offence?” and put it to him that yesterday he had said the offence of treason is in section 39(2)(e) of the Penal Code Act, then read out the words with which he is charged, noting he had by then been in prison for 182 days, and asked whether those words appear in the charge sheet.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: Answered “It is a treason offence” and confirmed “Yes” that the offence of treason is in section 39(2)(e) of the Penal Code Act; when asked to read the section replied “You just read it yourself”; and said of the words read out: “What you have read is not there, but it is in my cautioned statement.”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked repeatedly whether the charge sheet contains the word “Government”, the words Dar es Salaam City Council, Kinondoni, Ubungo, Temeke, the President of the United Republic of Tanzania Samia Suluhu Hassan, the Vice-President Dr Philip Mpango, any title of a leader of any level of government, the name of any government authority such as Mchafukoge Street, or the Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner Albert Chalamila, and asked the judges that the witness answer in the manner in which he was being asked.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: Said the word Government is in the charge sheet — “Yes, if you read to the end you will see it” ; “I don't know how you are interpreting it? It is there” ; “They are there” — but said the words Dar es Salaam City Council, Kinondoni, Ubungo and Temeke are not there, “not even Kigamboni Municipality is there”, and that the names of President Samia Suluhu Hassan and Vice-President Dr Philip Mpango, any title of a leader of any level, any government authority, and Regional Commissioner Albert Chalamila are not in the alleged treasonous statements.

a639.speaker: Judge Dunstan Ndunguru, Judge in Charge of the High Court Sub-Registry of Iringa (head of the panel)
a639.name: Judge Dunstan Ndunguru
a639.title: Judge in Charge of the High Court Sub-Registry of Iringa (head of the panel)
a639.speech: “If the witness says they are there, and you say they are not there, and the court has the charge sheet, then the court itself has the duty to determine whether they are there or not.”

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: Defined Government: “Serikali comes from a Persian word, which means authority, or it is the people and institutions within society that hold administrative authority. There are also rules that are followed in order to protect the existing rules and procedures” ; read Article 151(1) of the Constitution of the United Republic: “Government means the Government of the United Republic, the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, and any person exercising authority on behalf of the Government.”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Put it to the witness that the people who directed him to open the treason file were the DCI, Ramadhani Kingai, and the DCP, Ramadhani Ng'anzi.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: “I was not directed; I myself opened it after seeing that the investigation was sufficient.”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked in how many big political cases or cases of public importance the witness had conducted investigations in his 22 years in the Police Force, asked him to name them, and asked whether any case he investigated had ever reached its conclusion with a judgment delivered by a court.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: Said he had handled four such cases, naming that of Dr Willibrod Slaa (saying “I don't know where it ended up”), that of Lembeli in Kahama, and that of John Heche in Tarime, which “was withdrawn by nolle prosequi”; said that in 22 years no case he investigated had reached its conclusion with a judgment — “There is none, but that of Tundu Lissu will reach its conclusion.”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked why the witness said the words he spoke on the day he called journalists were a treason offence, and whether calling journalists to listen to you is itself a treason offence, stating that the intention of treason must be shown by acts or publications or drawings.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: “Yes, they were a treason offence” ; on whether calling journalists is a treason offence: “It depends” ; agreed that the intention of treason must be shown by acts, publications or drawings: “That is correct.”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked who posted the words on the Jambo TV network and why the protected witness P had not been charged, whether he is one of the directors of Jambo TV, whether he has the password of the Jambo TV network, and, if so, how he had entered the network and posted the moving pictures.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: Said of who broadcast the words on the network: “It is P and Tundu Lissu”; said P has not been charged “because he is a journalist and he did not come to you at your meeting in order to put the information in his kitchen”, adding that P had told them that after the meeting of the Chadema Chairman, the journalists were taken out of the hall; said he was not certain whether Lissu is one of the directors of Jambo TV, that he cannot know whether Lissu has the network password, and “I don't know” how the pictures were posted.

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked where the meeting with journalists was held, and whether the witness had questioned John Mnyika or the Chadema Information Officer, Brenda Rupia, or other Chadema leaders about the procedure for inviting journalists, putting it to him: “But it is me you have fixed upon?”

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: Said “I don't know” where the meeting was held and, pressed on investigating the case without knowing, replied “You did not invite us”; said he did not question John Mnyika or Brenda Rupia and “We did not question” other Chadema leaders; and answered “Yes” when asked whether it was Lissu alone he had fixed upon.

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked whether the witness sought advice from lawyers when writing the statement, who told him he was allowed to write his own cautioned statement, who cautioned him and who certified the statement he wrote.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: “I did not seek advice” ; “There is no law or section preventing me from writing my statement” ; “It is the law that cautioned me” ; “I myself am the one who cautioned myself” ; “I myself [certified it], because there is no law preventing me.”

a639.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.name: Tundu Lissu
a639.title: Chadema Chairman and accused (defending himself, cross-examination)
a639.speech: Asked whether, since leaving the JKT (National Service), he has been employed by the JKT, and whether reserve soldiers have the same conditions as others regarding joining political parties.

a639.speaker: ACP George Bagyemu, Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.name: ACP George Bagyemu
a639.title: Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations, Dar es Salaam Special Zone (first prosecution witness)
a639.speech: “You have not been employed, but you are a reserve soldier” ; on whether reserve soldiers have the same conditions as others on joining political parties: “I do not know.”

a794.speaker: Ghana AIDS Commission
a794.name: Ghana AIDS Commission
a794.speech: Has expressed worry about continued stigma, discrimination and human rights abuses which persons living with HIV suffer from in Ghanaian society; according to the Commission the trend which is entrenched in communities pushes many persons who live with the disease into hiding thereby not accessing the much-needed healthcare.

a794.speaker: Dr. Fred Nana Poku, Director Technical Services at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a794.name: Dr. Fred Nana Poku
a794.title: Director Technical Services at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a794.speech: Rallied support of the media to shed light on the disease and especially means of spread to cause attitudinal change amongst citizens; he was unhappy that persons living with HIV continue to suffer stigma, discrimination and human rights abuses and asked the media to lead the charge in demystifying some myths and misconceptions surrounding the disease ; "The media is a very important platform to reach numerous people because they are pluralistic and they have the influence. So we decided to engage them in this training session on the myths and misconceptions about HIV and the human right abuses that goes on"

a794.speaker: Dr. Fred Nana Poku, Director Technical Services at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a794.name: Dr. Fred Nana Poku
a794.title: Director Technical Services at the Ghana AIDS Commission
a794.speech: Asked persons who live with HIV to follow strictly with their medication to ensure their general well-being; he said the Ghana AIDS Commission will work round the clock to ensure HIV is no longer a public health threat.

a794.speaker: Zohra Baisara, USAID Ghana Health Office Director
a794.name: Zohra Baisara
a794.title: USAID Ghana Health Office Director
a794.speech: Touting the role of the media in Ghana's HIV and AIDS response, was confident that the training will improve understanding of journalists for accurate reportage, which she noted would better equip them to support broader engagement with policy makers and the public; she said accurate reportage will prevent misinformation and support community education to reduce stigma ; "We believe that journalists play an important role in shaping public perceptions about HIV and AIDS, because of this the media cannot be left out of our efforts to educate citizens"

a794.speaker: Dominic Hlodzi, National Organizer of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA)
a794.name: Dominic Hlodzi
a794.title: National Organizer of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA)
a794.speech: Encouraged beneficiary journalists to impact knowledge acquired to other colleagues and pledged commitment of the GJA to look for other training opportunities for journalists ; "Discrimination and stigmatization are sending person's living with HIV to their graves and we have to stop that. We are expecting the participants to do a lot more on their stories relating to HIV and AIDS particularly about stigma and discrimination, so that what we aim to achieve that is ending stigmatization will be achieved"

a794.speaker: Rebecca Ekpe, Public Affairs Officer/Spokesperson of the Ghana Journalists Association
a794.name: Rebecca Ekpe
a794.title: Public Affairs Officer/Spokesperson of the Ghana Journalists Association
a794.speech: Commended PEPFAR, Send-Ghana and its partners for organising the training to equip journalists; urged beneficiary journalists to work hard to promote the success stories of persons living with HIV, the effectiveness of antiretroviral medicines (ARVs) and the need to end all forms of stigmatization and discrimination while highlighting the work of the GAC and its partners ; "As communicators, we help shape the minds and actions of many people by using innovative ways to surmount these health challenges. Together we can help to destigmatize HIV and AIDS and that can also contribute significantly to curbing the spread of this disease"

a981.speaker: Somaliland lawmakers visiting Finland (delegation)
a981.name: Somaliland lawmakers visiting Finland (delegation)
a981.speech: Urged Helsinki to redirect development aid directly to Somaliland after Finland suspended funding to Somalia over refugee repatriations and concerns of mismanagement.

a981.speaker: Ali Hamud Jibril, Deputy Speaker of Somaliland’s House of Representatives
a981.name: Ali Hamud Jibril
a981.title: Deputy Speaker of Somaliland’s House of Representatives
a981.speech: Said they requested that Somaliland receive the future assistance Finland had previously allocated to Somalia; noted Finland provided €54 million over the past four years, but Somaliland saw little of it. ; Argued Somaliland could deliver stronger results: “We explained that our projects begin and end on schedule.” “Finland expressed frustration with Somalia’s handling of aid and said more progress could have been made if Somaliland had been the recipient.”

a981.speaker: Finnish officials
a981.name: Finnish officials
a981.speech: Echoed concerns that Somali authorities mishandled donor funds and failed to complete projects.

a981.speaker: Finland (government)
a981.name: Finland (government)
a981.speech: Has previously confirmed that Somalia’s refusal to cooperate on refugee returns was a key factor in the aid freeze.

a981.speaker: The Somaliland delegation
a981.name: The Somaliland delegation
a981.speech: Said they are not seeking to accept refugees and did not raise the matter in Helsinki.

a1198.speaker: Russia (formal request to NATO for security guarantees)
a1198.name: Russia (formal request to NATO for security guarantees)
a1198.speech: In the request by Russia on NATO to hold talks with its on-security guarantees, Russia made it loud and clear that admission of Ukraine into NATO is a dark red line that must not to be crossed. It gave reasons that the implication of having NATO bases in Ukraine would neutralize its own nuclear deterrence since it would not have enough time to react to any missile fired from Kiev that takes few minutes to reach Moscow. Russia even went as far as submitting a framework proposal to negotiate upon that would guarantee that Ukraine will remain neutral and never be admitted into NATO.

a1198.speaker: 2001 Ukraine census
a1198.name: 2001 Ukraine census
a1198.speech: According to the 2001 Ukraine census, individuals who identify themselves as ethnic Russians accounted for 17.3% of the population of Ukraine.

a1198.speaker: Anthony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a1198.name: Anthony Blinken
a1198.title: US Secretary of State
a1198.speech: During a news conference in Berlin with his German counterpart, Secretary of State Anthony Blinken warns that any invasion and act of aggression will be met with a swift, severe, and united response.

a1277.speaker: Femi Otedola, Nigerian oil magnate (memoir "Making It Big: Lessons from a Life in Business")
a1277.name: Femi Otedola
a1277.title: Nigerian oil magnate (memoir "Making It Big: Lessons from a Life in Business")
a1277.speech: has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo insulted him, cursed him out, and nearly threw him under the bus in 2004 after a nationwide diesel scarcity erupted following a controversial deregulation move; he revealed that it was his idea to deregulate the diesel market. "When President Obasanjo deregulated diesel in 2004, Zenon took an unassailable lead in the market. My opponents' reaction was to tell the president that we'd turned the market upside down [and that the] economy was about to be brought down because there was no diesel, and Obasanjo was mad at me because he'd sought and received assurances from us that NNPC's exit from diesel importation wouldn't affect supply. My critics then fanned the flames by telling him there was no diesel in the country, that trucks couldn't move, and that industries were shutting down." ; "As soon as Obasanjo saw me, he flew into a rage again... I allowed him to cool down, and when he stopped talking, I tried to explain the situation. 'Baba, they're lying to you. It's all lies. I have six ships waiting to discharge big supplies of diesel.'" ; "I was even paying demurrage. I told the president that I was the victim of competitors' backbiting", saying he asked Obasanjo to "see what they come up with next… You'll see that it's me who's telling you the truth." ; "I knew it was people in NNPC – the state monopoly, in their now–teetering positions of power, who were against deregulation – who'd been telling him these lies. They wanted to continue to import, and rake in the subsidy money." ; "Obasanjo was a determined and robust president. Jealous people did not easily sway him. Once he made up his mind that someone was trustworthy and genuine, as he seemed to do about me that day, he stopped listening to the naysayers."

a1277.speaker: Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President (as quoted by Otedola)
a1277.name: Olusegun Obasanjo
a1277.title: former Nigerian President (as quoted by Otedola)
a1277.speech: "You're a stupid boy! God will punish you! You persuaded me to deregulate diesel, and now there's no diesel in the country!" ; "What kind of rubbish is this? What kind of nonsense is this?"

a1326.speaker: Siboniso Masilela, Under Secretary, representing Principal Secretary Thabsile Mlangeni, Ministry of Economic Planning and Development
a1326.name: Siboniso Masilela
a1326.title: Under Secretary, representing Principal Secretary Thabsile Mlangeni, Ministry of Economic Planning and Development
a1326.speech: Warmly opened and blessed the workshop, highlighting the government's unwavering dedication to transparency, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making ; extended his sincere welcome and thanked the attendees for their commitment to the process, underscoring the collective importance of the initiative.

a1326.speaker: Nokwazi Mathebula, Consultant
a1326.name: Nokwazi Mathebula
a1326.title: Consultant
a1326.speech: Under her expert guidance, key stakeholders meticulously revisited the objectives of the M&E Policy, a review that ensured the policy remained fully aligned with the long-term aspirations and immediate needs of the nation.

a1326.speaker: Participants at the validation workshop
a1326.name: Participants at the validation workshop
a1326.speech: Actively shared their insights and provided essential feedback, repeatedly highlighting the importance of creating a policy that not only sets clear expectations but also genuinely empowers all ministries to collaborate effectively ; expressed their deep gratitude for the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to such a significant national initiative.

a1326.speaker: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) country programme document for Eswatini (2016-2020)
a1326.name: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) country programme document for Eswatini (2016-2020)
a1326.speech: Identified priorities for UNDP's interventions that were highly relevant to the country's development challenges, established around objectives in line with the National Development Strategy 2013-2022, the King's Vision 2022 and the United Nations Development Assistance Framework outcomes, with Eswatini planning to contribute to outcomes on inclusive economic growth and sustainable development, and on resilience and risk reduction incorporating sustainable natural resource management and good governance, equity and citizen participation; although activities implemented by UNDP have too often deviated from its set objectives and planned outputs.

a1363.speaker: Government of Lesotho
a1363.name: Government of Lesotho
a1363.speech: "has lauded the World Food Programme (WFP) for its assistance in addressing food and nutrition needs in Lesotho during periods of food insecurity, climatic, and economic shocks" and "acclaimed WFP for strengthening Lesotho's humanitarian response capacity, disaster risk management, and early warning systems, and for increasing accountability and access to data through the development of a geospatial platform."

a1363.speaker: Dr Retšilisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a1363.name: Dr Retšilisitsoe Matlanyane
a1363.title: Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a1363.speech: Expressed satisfaction with the conspicuous achievements under the preceding Country Strategic Plan, saying the achievements were a testament to the impact that WFP continued to radiate in Basotho's lives: "WFP assisted the government to address food and nutrition needs during the periods of food insecurity, climatic and economic shocks; strengthen its capacities in humanitarian response, disaster risk management, and early warning systems; increase accountability and access to data through the development of a geospatial platform" ; said the partnership had also been very instrumental in the success of the primary school feeding programme ; "The transition by WFP from direct implementation to strengthening systems and providing technical assistance to the government and key stakeholders to enhance capacities to manage and implement national programmes is worth ululation."

a1363.speaker: Dr Retšilisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a1363.name: Dr Retšilisitsoe Matlanyane
a1363.title: Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a1363.speech: Added that WFP, in collaboration with the government, had formed a taskforce to mobilise resources for the second-generation Country Strategic Plan (2024-2029); indicated that resource mobilisation was indispensable as the agency did not have a core budget but worked on a voluntary basis with various donors; said the total budget for the CSP is USD$95 million (over M1.6 billion) with a current shortfall of USD$78 [million], and called for concerted support from other development partners and the private sector to assist in filling the gap ; "In addition, the taskforce will support the government to unlock potential funding opportunities by exploring untapped funding streams, diversifying the donor's base, and exploring innovative finance solutions."

a1363.speaker: Dr Retšilisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a1363.name: Dr Retšilisitsoe Matlanyane
a1363.title: Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
a1363.speech: "WFP's strategic interventions as articulated in the CSP, align with Lesotho's extended National Strategic Development Plan II, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2024-2028)" ; said this alluded to the Principles of Harmonisation and Country Ownership, which were critical to ensure effective development cooperation ; "Fragmentation in Lesotho partners' interventions has contributed to dwarfed gains, despite huge investments that are being reported. I wish to urge our Partners (to go) for a more coordinated approach in your support, to avert the past inefficiencies and weak developmental outcomes."

a1363.speaker: Elliot Vhurumuku, WFP Country Director
a1363.name: Elliot Vhurumuku
a1363.title: WFP Country Director
a1363.speech: Indicated that in July 2024, WFP-Lesotho commenced the implementation of the new five-year CSP 2024-2029 that marked a strategic shift for WFP, transitioning from direct implementation to strengthening systems and providing technical assistance to the Government to enhance its capacities to manage and implement national programmes; said that at the time, the government had declared a national food insecurity disaster due to El Nino induced drought, effective in 2024, and asked for support from multi-sectoral partners and stakeholders in developing a National Response Plan ; "In response to the declaration, WFP consolidated plans and assisted people from rural areas of the most hard hit six districts (Qacha's Nek, Maseru, Mohale's Hoek, Quthing, Berea, and Thaba Tseka) where close to half of the population needed humanitarian assistance" ; "WFP, in collaboration with UNICEF, supported the Ministry of Education and Training and the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition's implementation and monitoring of a home-grown school feeding programme that integrates WASH, child protection and health interventions" ; indicated that they had also worked with the Disaster Management Authority (DMA) at national and district levels and identified eligible people for support and ensured that the right people received assistance.

a1363.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations of Lesotho
a1363.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a1363.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations of Lesotho
a1363.speech: Called for continuous accountability and transparency and underscored the importance of a more targeted approach when WFP selects beneficiaries: "It should be in a manner that does not lead to moral hazard and which is sustainable. There should be deliberate efforts to ensure that the recipients graduate and do not become perpetual dependents. The economic challenges facing our country have been resonated frequently both at the micro and macro levels" ; noted these challenges had been compounded by the evolving development financing landscape due to multifaceted factors such as climate conditions, geo-political conflicts, pandemics, and the recent trade policy conflicts that have had an excruciating impact on the economy; and noted that growing global uncertainties and risks continued to threaten development progress and sustainable finance prospects.

a1363.speaker: Amanda Khozi-Mkwashi, UN Resident Coordinator
a1363.name: Amanda Khozi-Mkwashi
a1363.title: UN Resident Coordinator
a1363.speech: Reaffirmed UN agencies' support as technical partners of the government; said WFP aims to enhance climate-resilient food systems, human capital, social protection and emergency preparedness and response, while prioritising vulnerable groups at risk ; "This CSP is aligned with all three pillars of the 2024-2028 United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework and the Government's economic and institutional transformation."

a1523.speaker: Experts gathered in Dakar (workshop participants)
a1523.name: Experts gathered in Dakar (workshop participants)
a1523.speech: Issue an urgent call to lift barriers linked to pharmaceutical patents, which they say is essential to achieving universal health coverage in Senegal; they advocated greater use of the flexibilities provided for by the TRIPS Agreement, such as compulsory licences or participation in the Medicines Patent Pool.

a1523.speaker: Dr Karim Diop
a1523.name: Dr Karim Diop
a1523.speech: Stressed that "access to medicines is a pillar of Universal Health Coverage (UHC), but financial and logistical barriers threaten this objective"; he notably pointed to the disengagement of USAID, which funded 42.7% of the HIV response, creating a gap of 9 billion CFA francs ; "Millions of people on ARVs are threatened by treatment interruptions", he warned.

a1523.speaker: Dr Karim Diop
a1523.name: Dr Karim Diop
a1523.speech: Insisted, on financing: "The 2025 budget shows a critical gap of 14 million euros for the fight against HIV. The State must prioritise these expenditures within the framework of universal health coverage."

a1523.speaker: Prof. Papa Gallo Sow
a1523.name: Prof. Papa Gallo Sow
a1523.speech: Revealed that "certain anticancer medicines or second-line ARVs are still under patent, limiting competition and keeping prices high" ; "Senegal must actively negotiate in international forums to broaden access to essential medicines", he insisted.

a1523.speaker: Prof. Papa Gallo Sow
a1523.name: Prof. Papa Gallo Sow
a1523.speech: Explained that SEN-PNA (the National Supply Pharmacy), although central to the supply chain, faces "long administrative delays and unpaid receivables" ; on pooled procurement he stressed: "Group purchasing has already made it possible to bring the price of ARVs down to $2.70 per unit. This strategy must be extended to other critical medicines."

a1523.speaker: Prof. Papa Gallo Sow
a1523.name: Prof. Papa Gallo Sow
a1523.speech: Noted on local production: "Local production of Dolutegravir or Sofosbuvir would be a game-changer for reducing costs and delays" ; concluded: "Guaranteeing equitable access to medicines is not only a health issue, but one of social justice."

a1523.speaker: Study on supply mechanisms, prices and volumes of tracer medicines in Senegal (ENDA Sante / Kelin / ITPC Global)
a1523.name: Study on supply mechanisms
a1523.title: prices and volumes of tracer medicines in Senegal (ENDA Sante / Kelin / ITPC Global)
a1523.speech: Recommends increased digitalisation of processes, notably via the WAMBO platform already used for ARV purchases; it also documents that Senegal faces a double epidemiological burden and a dependence on imports (95% of medicines), 93% therapeutic coverage for antiretrovirals, and persistent stock-outs, delivery delays and prohibitive costs.

a1523.speaker: Workshop participants (roadmap proposal)
a1523.name: Workshop participants (roadmap proposal)
a1523.speech: In the short term called for an urgent simplification of procurement procedures and the creation of an emergency fund dedicated to vital medicines; for the medium term placed emphasis on strengthening SEN-PNA's operational capacities through advanced digital tools; and for the long term on local pharmaceutical production, intensified regional group purchasing, and sustained advocacy for optimal use of TRIPS flexibilities.

a1780.speaker: Mossi Salou, Secretary General of the Presidency of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP)
a1780.name: Mossi Salou
a1780.title: Secretary General of the Presidency of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP)
a1780.speech: Announced that the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) had officially handed back a significant quantity of equipment and logistical resources to the State of Niger following the end of its project, at a press conference held on 18 July 2024.

a1780.speaker: Mossi Salou, Secretary General of the Presidency of the CNSP
a1780.name: Mossi Salou
a1780.title: Secretary General of the Presidency of the CNSP
a1780.speech: Stressed that the CNSP is committed to ensuring transparency and traceability in the distribution of the goods received, noting that the handover was meticulously documented in a report under the supervision of the bailiff, thereby guaranteeing that the equipment will be allocated to the identified beneficiaries according to the procedures established by the competent services of the Presidency of the CNSP.

a1780.speaker: Mohamed Kamil Agali, representative of the Director General of MCA-Niger
a1780.name: Mohamed Kamil Agali
a1780.title: representative of the Director General of MCA-Niger
a1780.speech: Specified that this handover is part of the normal MCA closure process, planned and not linked to any specific event, including that of 26 July 2023.

a1780.speaker: Presidency of the CNSP
a1780.name: Presidency of the CNSP
a1780.speech: Welcomes the successes of the MCC in Niger and salutes the pragmatism of this cooperation, which has brought significant benefits to the country's rural populations.

a1792.speaker: WikiLeaks classified United States diplomatic cable (document)
a1792.name: WikiLeaks classified United States diplomatic cable (document)
a1792.speech: Exposed how Nigerian legal luminary Chief Afe Babalola and former president Olusegun Obasanjo in 2004 allegedly purchased a Court of Appeal ruling that ensured the then Adamawa State governor, Boni Haruna, remained in office ; the summary stated: "On July 5, an appeals court sitting in Jos overturned the March 24 election tribunal decision that had nullified the election of Adamawa State Governor Boni Haruna. The verdicts of the appeals court and the election tribunal differed so significantly on their findings of the relevant facts that they beg the question of whether one verdict or the other may have been 'influenced' by outside parties. End summary." ; noted that the original election tribunal had found "beyond reasonable doubt" that electoral malpractices had taken place, and that the election was noncompliant with the Electoral Law ; that the appeals court in Jos found the evidence used by the election tribunal was "absolutely inadequate even to prove the simplest of a criminal offence, very impotent to affect the appellants/cross respondents, ridiculous for convicting any of the appellants/cross respondents with commission of any electoral offence," and that the evidence was scandalous and naive as a basis for nullifying the election ; "Note. The appeals court decision is final and cannot be appealed to Nigeria's Supreme Court. End Note." ; "Comment. While the Embassy has been unable to examine the Appeal Court ruling in its entirety, the verdicts of the appeals court and the election tribunal differed so significantly on their findings of the relevant facts that it begs the question of whether one verdict or the other may have been 'influenced' by outside parties. Both courts were composed of senior members of the judiciary, both operating under the same laws, principles, and guidelines. It would be normal for an appeals court to have a slightly different interpretation than a lower court, but the radically divergent views of the Jos court from the Yola tribunal leave little doubt that something other than the law was factored in to the final decision." The cable was classified by Russells J Hanks, acting Political counsellor.

a1792.speaker: Attorney for then Governor Boni Haruna, who works for Presidential attorney Afe Babalola (anonymous, cited in the US cable)
a1792.name: Attorney for then Governor Boni Haruna
a1792.title: who works for Presidential attorney Afe Babalola (anonymous, cited in the US cable)
a1792.speech: Confirmed that the favourable ruling by the Court of Appeal "was ensured in typical Nigerian fashion: with cash" ; said that when President Obasanjo sent Babalola to take over the appeal, he also sent cash to be used for the appeal ; claimed that he went along for the delivery of 30 million naira (about $225,000) to each of the five judges on the tribunal but did not know if this was all the money disbursed: "This is the normal procedure when it is an important case," he averred.

a1792.speaker: Omoyele Sowore, human rights activist and Convener of the #RevolutionNow movement (post on X)
a1792.name: Omoyele Sowore
a1792.title: human rights activist and Convener of the #RevolutionNow movement (post on X)
a1792.speech: Said "Babalola's chickens are coming home to roost." ; "Chief Afe Babalola's chickens are coming home to roost! Facts are now emerging that, in fact, the reputation they are using the Nigeria Police Force to protect by kidnapping Dele Farotimi doesn't exist at all. Here is a Wikileaks US government cable detailing how Chief Afe and former President Obasanjo bought a Court of Appeal judgment with cash in Plateau state. #FreeDeleFarotimiNow"

a1792.speaker: WikiLeaks (statement on its website)
a1792.name: WikiLeaks (statement on its website)
a1792.speech: Said it was to publish 251,287 cables, originating from 274 embassies and dating from December 28, 1966, to February 28, 2010.

a1792.speaker: SaharaReporters (earlier reports)
a1792.name: SaharaReporters (earlier reports)
a1792.speech: Reported last Tuesday that Farotimi was arrested and taken to Ekiti State for allegedly defaming Afe Babalola, a prominent legal figure, in his book "Nigeria and Its Criminal Justice System" ; had reported that Farotimi, currently in remand, filed an application for his bail at the Ado Ekiti Magisterial District of Magistrate Court of Nigeria.

a1792.speaker: Abayomi Adeosun, presiding magistrate (court record)
a1792.name: Abayomi Adeosun
a1792.title: presiding magistrate (court record)
a1792.speech: Had denied Farotimi bail and ordered that he be remanded in the correctional centre until December 10 for further hearing.

a1792.speaker: Dele Farotimi's counsel, 11 lawyers led by Prof. O.F Emiri, SAN (bail application, Charge No: MAD/1476/2024)
a1792.name: Dele Farotimi's counsel
a1792.title: 11 lawyers led by Prof. O.F Emiri, SAN (bail application, Charge No: MAD/1476/2024)
a1792.speech: Sought among others "an order admitting the Applicant to bail pending the determination of his trial before this Honourable Court. Any other orders this Honourable court may deem fit to make in the circumstance." The application was brought "pursuant to section 36(5) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, Article 6 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights and Sections 158 of the Administration of Criminal Justice ACT 2015 and under the inherent jurisdiction of the Honourable Court." The lawyers gave four grounds: "1. the Defendant/Applicant is presumed innocent until proven guilty as guaranteed under Section 36(5) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (1999) and Article 6 of the African Charter on Human and People's Rights. 2. The offences alleged are bailable under the Criminal Code Act. 3. The Defendant/Applicant has a fixed address, is a lawyer with 25 years of experience and is a prominent member of the society, posing no flight risk. 4. The Defendant/Applicant undertakes to be available for trial and comply with all conditions set by this Honourable Court."

a1792.speaker: Dele Farotimi, human rights lawyer (court arraignment)
a1792.name: Dele Farotimi
a1792.title: human rights lawyer (court arraignment)
a1792.speech: Pleaded "not guilty" to the 16 charges brought against him when he was arraigned at a Magistrates court in Ado-Ekiti on Wednesday.

a1932.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (statement sent to the newsroom)
a1932.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (statement sent to the newsroom)
a1932.speech: According to a statement sent to our newsroom, the signing of the Financing Agreement between the Governments of Mozambique and the United States, through the MCC, is scheduled for September of this year in Washington DC.

a2271.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development in Liberia (USAID) and the Government of Liberia (press release)
a2271.name: U.S. Agency for International Development in Liberia (USAID) and the Government of Liberia (press release)
a2271.speech: Officially announced the launch of the Local Health Solutions (LHS) Activity, a five-year initiative aimed at strengthening Liberia's health system, designed to improve the delivery of affordable, equitable, and high-quality healthcare services by fostering local leadership and supporting local organizations in strengthening health systems; the Activity will promote inclusive governance structures, strengthen supply chain management, enhance data use, and improve the quality of services, including maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health, malaria services, and laboratory and disease surveillance systems.

a2271.speaker: Mark Toner, U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a2271.name: Mark Toner
a2271.title: U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a2271.speech: "This initiative goes beyond healthcare—it's about building resilience and ensuring that communities have the leadership and tools they need to thrive." ; "The United States is proud to work alongside Liberia to improve the quality of health for all, particularly in the most underserved areas."

a2637.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, African Union Commission leader/Chairperson
a2637.name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
a2637.title: African Union Commission leader/Chairperson
a2637.speech: Unveiling the statue at a ceremony attended by numerous African heads of state, said: “The legacy of this remarkable leader encapsulates the essence of Pan Africanism, profound wisdom, and service to Africa.” He recalled Nyerere’s own comments at the inaugural OAU summit in 1963.

a2637.speaker: Julius Nyerere, former Tanzanian leader (at the inaugural OAU summit, 1963)
a2637.name: Julius Nyerere
a2637.title: former Tanzanian leader (at the inaugural OAU summit, 1963)
a2637.speech: “Our continent is one, and we are all Africans.”

a2637.speaker: Julius Nyerere, former Tanzanian leader
a2637.name: Julius Nyerere
a2637.title: former Tanzanian leader
a2637.speech: Defended the absence of multi-party elections by declaring that Tanzanians had far more freedom under him than they had ever had under British rule, and that the one-party system was vital for stability.

a2637.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, Tanzania's President
a2637.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a2637.title: Tanzania's President
a2637.speech: Paying her tribute to Nyerere, said: “To him, Africa’s wellbeing came first, before popular approval, personal fortune or country wellbeing.”

a2637.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, Zambia's President (post on X)
a2637.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a2637.title: Zambia's President (post on X)
a2637.speech: Described the unveiling of the statue to “one of our continent’s iconic figures” as a “proud day”: “A proud day as we joined other #African leaders unveil the monument which honours 1 of our continent’s iconic figures, former President of Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere. Co-founder #OAU, Co-founder #SADC, Revolutionary leader, Pan Africanist.”

a2637.speaker: African Union (@_AfricanUnion, post on X)
a2637.name: African Union (@_AfricanUnion
a2637.title: post on X)
a2637.speech: “Statement By H.E. Mr. Moussa Faki Mahamat Chairperson of the African Union Commission at the Unveiling Ceremony of the Statue of the Late Julius Nyerere.”

a2637.speaker: African Union Political Affairs Peace and Security (@AUC_PAPS, post on X)
a2637.name: African Union Political Affairs Peace and Security (@AUC_PAPS
a2637.title: post on X)
a2637.speech: “Just unveiled: The statue of the former Tanzanian president, H.E. Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere, a leading pan-Africanist and peace builder, stands proudly in front of the Julius Nyerere Political Affairs, Peace & Security Building at @_AfricanUnion.”

a2637.speaker: William Samoei Ruto, Kenya's President (post on X)
a2637.name: William Samoei Ruto
a2637.title: Kenya's President (post on X)
a2637.speech: “Today, the African Union honoured former Tanzanian President Julius Nyerere, one of the founding fathers of independent Africa, by unveiling his statue at the AU headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Even after Tanzania became independent in 1961, President Nyerere was of the…”

a2637.speaker: DIRCO South Africa (@DIRCO_ZA, post on X)
a2637.name: DIRCO South Africa (@DIRCO_ZA
a2637.title: post on X)
a2637.speech: “#DYK? | Mr Julius Kambarage Nyerere translated two Shakespearean plays into Swahili. Today, Africa leaders witnessed the unveiling of the statue of former President of the United Republic of Tanzania, the late Julius Kambarage Nyerere at the AUC compound.”

a2637.speaker: Encyclopaedia Britannica (cited)
a2637.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica (cited)
a2637.speech: According to the Encyclopaedia Britannica, he was a trained teacher and became the first person from Tanganyika to study at a British university, when he went to study in Edinburgh in 1949.

a2793.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a2793.title: President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.speech: Declared that the North, which gave him over half a million votes in 2020, would not be forgotten. “Boma ili silanga, ndi voti yanu — likuyendetsedwa ndi inu. Zomwe zachitika pano ndi ntchito ya voti yomwe munandipatsa” (“This government is not mine, it is your vote — it is run by you. What has happened here is the work of the vote you gave me”), he said emphatically, reminding the crowd that his presidency was made possible by the overwhelming support from Northern voters. ; “Ngati munandivotera mu 2020, mukuwona kale ntchito. Sindikuyankhula za malonjezo — ndikuyankhula za zomwe zawonekera” (“If you voted for me in 2020, you can already see the work. I am not talking about promises — I am talking about what is visible”), Chakwera declared, reinforcing that his government is one of delivery, not deception.

a2793.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a2793.title: President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.speech: Unveiled an ambitious second-term development agenda for the North, including a new international airport in Mzuzu, Mmbelwa University and a network of major roads which, he said, will not only ease transport but “open the North to hot markets and private investment.” He also announced the creation of a Job Creation Fund and a Youth Innovation Fund growing from K2 billion to K5 billion, a “Ten-Ten Challenge” promising K10 million in capital to 10,000 youth-led businesses, tax relief of 10% for workers and small businesses, a push to connect 70% of Malawians to electricity, and microcredit access to electricity and water units.

a2793.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a2793.title: President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.speech: Promised to overhaul public governance by eliminating corruption at the service level. “Ndikubwera ndi njira yosiya kulipira ndi cash mmaofesi aboma kuti ziphuphu zithe” (“I am bringing a way to stop paying with cash in government offices so that corruption ends”), he said, vowing to end cash-based payments and ensure transparency. He also promised to introduce direct mayoral elections in Mzuzu and to appoint at least four cabinet ministers under the age of 35.

a2793.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a2793.title: President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.speech: Unveiled the “Tsogolo Account” initiative — a universal savings scheme for every Malawian child, with the government investing K500,000 per newborn from a Sovereign Wealth Fund. “Ana amenewa akhala oyamba osakhalamo waumphawi” (“These children will be the first not to live in poverty”), he said. He also pledged to increase the Constituency Development Fund to K500 million per constituency and introduce 72 new public services.

a2793.speaker: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera, President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.name: Lazarus McCarthy Chakwera
a2793.title: President of Malawi and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) leader
a2793.speech: Ending his address with an emotional appeal, Chakwera said, “Musagwedezeke. Musatekeseke. Musanamizidwe. Voti yanu ndiyomweyo chifukwa boma ndilomweli” (“Do not be shaken. Do not be swayed. Do not be deceived. Your vote is the same because the government is the same”).

a2795.speaker: US ambassador Michael J. Adler and Kate Crawford, US Agency for International Development
a2795.name: US ambassador Michael J. Adler and Kate Crawford
a2795.title: US Agency for International Development
a2795.speech: Have announced $95 million in additional humanitarian assistance from the American people to South Sudan.

a2795.speaker: US Embassy/USAID statement to Eye Radio
a2795.name: US Embassy/USAID statement to Eye Radio
a2795.speech: A statement to Eye Radio newsroom stated that the “funding will provide life-saving support to humanitarian partners, including the World Food Program, to continue to deliver critical food and nutrition assistance to more than 700,000 people in the most food-insecure areas of the country.” ; “These individuals are often arriving in South Sudan food-insecure, malnourished, and with few to no possessions,” reads the statement, adding that “as many as 3.3 million people may be adversely affected by flooding across South Sudan in the coming months.”

a2795.speaker: US ambassador Michael J. Adler and Kate Crawford, US Agency for International Development
a2795.name: US ambassador Michael J. Adler and Kate Crawford
a2795.title: US Agency for International Development
a2795.speech: According to the diplomat and USAID Director the assistance arrives at a critical time when “more than seven million people in South Sudan are facing high levels of acute food insecurity.”

a2795.speaker: US ambassador Michael J. Adler and Kate Crawford, US Agency for International Development
a2795.name: US ambassador Michael J. Adler and Kate Crawford
a2795.title: US Agency for International Development
a2795.speech: The duo urged the transitional government to do its part and contribute financial assistance to the humanitarian coffers. “In the face of these challenges and increased strain on the humanitarian system, we continue to urge the transitional government to contribute more financial resources to humanitarian assistance and to reduce the costs and risks faced by donors and their implementing partners, who are seeking to help the South Sudanese people.”

a2850.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2850.name: Donald Trump
a2850.title: US President
a2850.speech: Announced that from January 20, 2025 there would be only two sexes in the country (female and male), while halting the funds that had been used to finance and support treatment and welfare for people who had changed sex in America and around the world.

a2850.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2850.name: Donald Trump
a2850.title: US President
a2850.speech: Announced the decision to halt aid and funding, saying that an assessment would be carried out of the use of American taxpayers’ money ; suspended all activities of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) while ordering an assessment of its operations and of the funds under it within 90 days.

a2850.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2850.name: Donald Trump
a2850.title: US President
a2850.speech: Announced the withdrawal of the United States from the World Health Organization.

a2850.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a2850.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a2850.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a2850.speech: Said Trump’s decision would affect the health and welfare of people around the world.

a2850.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2850.name: Donald Trump
a2850.title: US President
a2850.speech: Announced that he will officially change the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America ; said of the Panama Canal that the agreement had been that America would leave Panama to run it, but the country changed the arrangement and the canal is instead run by China, so America is taking it back ; announced his intention to change the ownership of Greenland, under Denmark’s administration, so that it comes under the United States.

a2850.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2850.name: Donald Trump
a2850.title: US President
a2850.speech: Announced sanctions on Mexico, Canada and China, in what he claimed was a fight against nations opposing his policy of removing immigrants, accompanied by a 25 percent tax on every product entering America from those nations.

a2850.speaker: Claudia Sheinbaum, President of Mexico, and Justin Trudeau, Prime Minister of Canada
a2850.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
a2850.title: President of Mexico, and Justin Trudeau, Prime Minister of Canada
a2850.speech: Announced a decision to impose sanctions on America in retaliation.

a2850.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2850.name: Donald Trump
a2850.title: US President
a2850.speech: Announced a plan to enable America to take control of the Gaza area and transform it from ruins into a “Riviera”, a tourist coast of the Middle East ; says the plan will be accomplished by sending troops if necessary, insisting on the departure of the Palestinians of Gaza to seek refuge in neighbouring countries.

a2853.speaker: Chimwemwe (not real name), sex worker from Zingwangwa Township, Blantyre
a2853.name: Chimwemwe (not real name)
a2853.title: sex worker from Zingwangwa Township, Blantyre
a2853.speech: Says the suspension of oral and injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) “is a death sentence” ; said she is now worried and fears for her future: “I have been taking PrEP for two years, giving me peace of mind because even if a customer insists on not using a condom, I know I am protected” ; said men who discard condoms offer irresistible hefty sums of money to sleep with them, further exacerbating her fears.

a2853.speaker: Elizabeth (not real name), sex worker from Chilobwe Township
a2853.name: Elizabeth (not real name)
a2853.title: sex worker from Chilobwe Township
a2853.speech: Said the suspension will likely result in her contracting HIV: “We are already stigmatised, marginalised and now we are being deprived of the one thing that can protect us from HIV.”

a2853.speaker: Several other sex workers from Lilongwe
a2853.name: Several other sex workers from Lilongwe
a2853.speech: Expressed similar fears, saying in the absence of PrEP, the majority will be at risk of contracting HIV.

a2853.speaker: Circular signed by Linley Chewere, director of the Directorate of HIV, STI and Viral Hepatitis, Ministry of Health
a2853.name: Circular signed by Linley Chewere
a2853.title: director of the Directorate of HIV, STI and Viral Hepatitis, Ministry of Health
a2853.speech: Says PrEP suspension is part of contingency measures following the temporary suspension of the President’s Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar) by its implementing partners ; “The following services are considered as of moderate/low priority and, therefore, may need to be reduced or discontinued if staffing/logistics dictate.”

a2853.speaker: National Aids Commission (NAC) data
a2853.name: National Aids Commission (NAC) data
a2853.speech: Recent data shows HIV prevalence is highest among the sex workers, drug users and transgenders ; figures show that as of December 2022, HIV prevalence among an estimated population of 39 000 sex workers was 49.9 percent, while among a population of 35 400 men who have sex with men it was 12.8 percent, and among a population of 8 400 who inject themselves with drugs the prevalence stood at 27.0 percent.

a2853.speaker: Maziko Matemba, health rights activist
a2853.name: Maziko Matemba
a2853.title: health rights activist
a2853.speech: Said on Tuesday the situation must be a wake-up call for Malawi and other low-income countries to do soul-searching when introducing programmes and products that are too donor-dependent so that rights of people accessing such services are respected ; “But also, donor countries should allow countries to introduce only sustainable health services in respecting the rights of people accessing them. It is also important for Malawi to consider adopting health financing reforms to fill gaps of the suspended services at short, medium and long-term.”

a2853.speaker: National Aids Commission (NAC) data on infection trends
a2853.name: National Aids Commission (NAC) data on infection trends
a2853.speech: Data shows new HIV infections have been reduced by 88 percent since the peak of the pandemic in 1993, as 15 630 people were newly-infected in 2022 compared to 130 880 people in 1993 ; shows that since 2010 new HIV infections have declined by 72 percent, that new infections among children declined by 82 percent since 2010, that women and girls accounted for 61 percent of all new infections in 2022, and that Aids-related deaths reduced by 85 percent since the peak in 2003.

a2853.speaker: National Aids Commission (NAC)
a2853.name: National Aids Commission (NAC)
a2853.speech: In April 2024, NAC attributed high HIV infection rate to tertiary institutions.

a2870.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a2870.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a2870.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a2870.speech: Said Tanzania is making significant strides in the fight against HIV/AIDS, with increased awareness, testing and the use of antiretroviral treatment (ART); said a recent survey revealed that 82.7 per cent of people aged 15 and above living with HIV are now aware of their HIV status, a 22 per cent increase from 61 per cent five years ago, that 97.9 per cent of those aware of their status have begun ART compared to 94 per cent five years ago, and that 94.3 per cent of individuals on ART have achieved viral suppression, up from 87 per cent five years ago. “These results show significant progress toward our goal of ending HIV/AIDS by 2030”

a2870.speaker: 2022/2023 HIV/AIDS indicators survey (referenced by Vice-President Mpango)
a2870.name: 2022/2023 HIV/AIDS indicators survey (referenced by Vice-President Mpango)
a2870.speech: Revealed that new HIV infections among adults aged 15 and above stand at 60,000 per year

a2870.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a2870.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a2870.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
a2870.speech: Emphasised the global HIV targets for 2025, known as the “95-95-95” goal, which aims for 95 per cent of people living with HIV to know their status, 95 per cent of those diagnosed to start treatment and 95 per cent of those on treatment to achieve viral suppression; called on the Tanzania Commission for AIDS (TACAIDS) to collaborate with sector ministries, stakeholders and the community to address the factors contributing to the spread of HIV; and commended the successful partnership between the government and various stakeholders, including the private sector, the Global Fund, PEPFAR and UN agencies, for their ongoing support in implementing HIV/AIDS programmes in Tanzania

a2870.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice-President of Tanzania
a2870.name: Dr Philip Mpango
a2870.title: Vice-President of Tanzania
