a2870.speech: Urged young people, particularly young girls, to protect themselves from new HIV infections, citing data that shows they are at a higher risk, and encouraged the public to embrace education campaigns aimed at changing behaviours, abandoning harmful cultural practices and continuing to take precautions against HIV. “The new infections are often driven by risky behaviours such as excessive alcohol consumption, unprotected sex, having multiple partners and drug abuse” ; stressed the need to eliminate the stigma surrounding people living with HIV, as this hinders their access to services like voluntary testing, counselling and ART, noting that such stigma leads to fear, preventing many from seeking the help they need

a2870.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a2870.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a2870.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a2870.speech: Spoke about the government's collaboration with stakeholders in continuing the third phase of the “TIMIZA MALENGO” project, which targets adolescent girls and young women in 42 local councils to help them economically and socially, reducing their vulnerability to HIV; said the government has come up with the DREAMS project, which aims to reduce HIV infections among adolescent girls and young women in 14 local councils

a2870.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a2870.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a2870.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a2870.speech: Addressed the country's reliance on external funding for HIV-related activities and introduced the HIV Response Sustainability Roadmap, a plan outlining national strategies to implement the HIV response using domestic resources, with ten key reforms to be carried out through collaboration between government ministries, institutions, the private sector and NGOs, aimed at ensuring the sustainability of HIV initiatives and eliminating HIV as a public health threat by 2030

a2870.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Minister for Health, Tanzania
a2870.name: Jenista Mhagama
a2870.title: Minister for Health, Tanzania
a2870.speech: Said that her ministry will continue working to integrate the response to HIV, sexually transmitted infections and hepatitis, given their similar transmission routes, and emphasised the development of a comprehensive strategy to address these issues and strengthen the health of Tanzanians

a2870.speaker: Leticia Maurice, Chairperson of the National Council of People Living with HIV
a2870.name: Leticia Maurice
a2870.title: Chairperson of the National Council of People Living with HIV
a2870.speech: Called for the elimination of stigma and drug abuse, which hinder the government's efforts to fight the scourge, and reaffirmed the council's commitment to strengthening services tailored to the needs of vulnerable groups

a2892.speaker: Daphna Shochat, representative of Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI)
a2892.name: Daphna Shochat
a2892.title: representative of Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI)
a2892.speech: “At this moment, it is especially important to call things by their name,” she said at a press conference in Jerusalem presenting the group's report analysing the medical situation in the enclave.

a2892.speaker: Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) report
a2892.name: Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) report
a2892.speech: According to the analysis, the medical consequences of the Israeli offensive meet the requirements for the situation to be considered genocide under the Geneva Convention.

a2892.speaker: Yuli Novak, executive director of B'Tselem
a2892.name: Yuli Novak
a2892.title: executive director of B'Tselem
a2892.speech: Considered that reality “leaves no alternative but to recognise the truth: Israel is committing genocide against the Palestinians of the Gaza Strip.” ; Novak described Israeli society as “capable of erasing people's humanity and losing all empathy and moral obligations” through a “long process of dehumanisation of the Palestinians.” “It is a terrifying combination of circumstances that leads us to the reality we all see today,” she added.

a2892.speaker: B'Tselem (report)
a2892.name: B'Tselem (report)
a2892.speech: Published a report documenting statements by politicians and senior military officials calling for the destruction of Palestinian society in Gaza; warned that Israel is replicating in the occupied West Bank what it learned in Gaza, though on a smaller scale; the group states that there is a risk that the genocide will spread to the entire Palestinian population.

a2892.speaker: Local non-governmental organisations (at the press conference)
a2892.name: Local non-governmental organisations (at the press conference)
a2892.speech: Stated that Israeli leaders are the main ones responsible for what is happening, but also accused the international community of not doing enough to stop the war.

a2892.speaker: Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch
a2892.name: Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch
a2892.speech: Had already denounced that Israel is committing genocide or “genocidal acts” in Gaza.

a2892.speaker: Gaza Health Ministry
a2892.name: Gaza Health Ministry
a2892.speech: According to the Gaza Health Ministry, almost 60,000 Palestinians have died and tens of thousands have been wounded during the Israeli offensive against Gaza that followed the 7 October 2023 attacks by the Islamist group Hamas.

a2892.speaker: Various NGOs and the UN
a2892.name: Various NGOs and the UN
a2892.speech: Consider that the aid distribution, carried out only by an entity controlled by Tel Aviv and supported by the United States and at specific locations, is insufficient; it has been marked by episodes of desperation, chaos and violence by Israeli forces.

a2926.speaker: Judge Amir Ali, US District Court in Washington
a2926.name: Judge Amir Ali
a2926.title: US District Court in Washington
a2926.speech: Ordered the Trump administration to immediately restore funding to US foreign aid and development programs; said the sudden freeze has resulted in sweeping damages to non-profits and other organisations that help carry out crucial US assistance internationally ; “[The Trump administration] have not offered any explanation for why a blanket suspension of all congressionally appropriated foreign aid, which set off a shockwave and upended contracts with thousands of nonprofit groups, businesses and others” ; added that lawyers for the administration had failed to show they had a “rational reason for disregarding the countless small and large businesses that would have to shutter programmes or shutter their businesses altogether.”

a2926.speaker: Trump administration (argument in court)
a2926.name: Trump administration (argument in court)
a2926.speech: Argued it had to shut down funding for the thousands of USAID aid programmes abroad to conduct a “thorough review” of each programme individually, and decide on whether or not it should be eliminated.

a2926.speaker: Foreign aid and development programmes and contractors (plaintiffs, the AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition and the Global Health Council)
a2926.name: Foreign aid and development programmes and contractors (plaintiffs
a2926.title: the AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition and the Global Health Council)
a2926.speech: Argued that a 90-day blanket funding freeze had negatively impacted them.

a2926.speaker: US President Donald Trump and Elon Musk, who runs the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2926.name: US President Donald Trump and Elon Musk
a2926.title: who runs the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2926.speech: Accuse the agency of being out of line with their agenda.

a2926.speaker: Aid groups
a2926.name: Aid groups
a2926.speech: Have described the cutoff of USAID funds for programmes abroad as a sudden and absolute cutoff.

a2926.speaker: US District Judge Carl Nichols
a2926.name: US District Judge Carl Nichols
a2926.speech: Said that his order halting the Trump administration’s plans to pull all but a fraction of USAID staffers off the job worldwide will stay in place for at least another week; ordered the extension after a nearly three-hour hearing, much of it focused on how employees were affected by Trump and Musk’s abrupt orders.

a3028.speaker: Leonardo Simão
a3028.name: Leonardo Simão
a3028.speech: “Sometimes attention is concentrated on unconstitutional regimes and the perspective of the bigger picture is lost, which is the fight against terrorism, where the situation is quite serious.” ; “What is most urgent is to fight terrorism. When we talk to the military regimes, they ask: do you want elections to be held in a territory dominated by terrorism, where it is not possible to carry out voter registration? Where it is not possible to campaign? So what kind of elections are we going to have, how representative will they be?” ; “Let us look at the security question first and then we will see about the rest.”

a3028.speaker: Leonardo Simão
a3028.name: Leonardo Simão
a3028.speech: Believes that the tensest phase of mistrust between partners and the military regimes has already passed: “I think the situation becomes more complex, but [cooperation] is not impossible. There is already a greater appetite among those countries [under military regimes] for dialogue.” ; “It is necessary to work with the regional organisation [ECOWAS] and, from there, with each one of the countries. There was a period, above all up to January of this year, of belligerent rhetoric, but I think that period is being left behind.” ; “greater possibilities for a dialogue that makes more sense. What I have been sensing, in regular contact with each of these countries, is that today there is greater serenity, and that opens space for dialogue.”

a3028.speaker: Leonardo Simão
a3028.name: Leonardo Simão
a3028.speech: Argued for commitment despite his optimism: “One cannot think that things move forward on their own. There has to be commitment, sometimes discreet commitment. One has to keep working with all the living forces - political, religious, traditional and others - so that there is stability in the region as an entry point. From there, everything else gets resolved.”

a3028.speaker: Leonardo Simão
a3028.name: Leonardo Simão
a3028.speech: Pointed out that terrorism is the most urgent but not the only challenge facing the African sub-region: “The first challenge is terrorism, the second is the humanitarian drama, the third is demographic - that is, the [life prospects of] young people - and the fourth is climate change.” ; said it is necessary to “contain terrorism where it is,” in the centre of the Sahel, blocking “the strategic objective of linking up with the [Atlantic] coast and with piracy.”

a3028.speaker: Leonardo Simão
a3028.name: Leonardo Simão
a3028.speech: “Every effort must be made to support these countries in containing terrorism, but, at the same time, to pay humanitarian attention.” ; “Unfortunately, financial support for humanitarian aid is in decline” in Africa, in the face of emergency needs in Ukraine and in Gaza ; “This scenario must be reversed.”

a3270.speaker: Boni Yayi, Head of State of Benin
a3270.name: Boni Yayi
a3270.title: Head of State of Benin
a3270.speech: Recalled in his state of the nation message delivered last Monday before the National Assembly in Porto-Novo that the year 2015 confirms the good performances recorded over the past few years.

a3270.speaker: Delegation of executive directors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3270.name: Delegation of executive directors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3270.speech: Acknowledged that the prudent policies of the country's authorities have contributed to solid macroeconomic results; however, stronger, sustainable and more inclusive growth is essential to reduce poverty, in the face of a more difficult environment, including the economic slowdown in neighbouring Nigeria.

a3270.speaker: Djibril Salifou, Director General of the Electricity Community of Benin (CEB)
a3270.name: Djibril Salifou
a3270.title: Director General of the Electricity Community of Benin (CEB)
a3270.speech: Said the start of construction of this mega-project to secure the electricity supply in reality marks the end of 30 years of dearth under successive governments which spared no effort in seeking partners for its financing.

a3270.speaker: Boni Yayi, Head of State of Benin
a3270.name: Boni Yayi
a3270.title: Head of State of Benin
a3270.speech: Made suggestions at the third India-Africa Forum Summit to boost economic relations between India and the African continent, saying the expertise acquired by India in various fields and the similarity of socio-economic realities with Africa predispose the continent to further develop a cooperation corresponding to the needs of African countries.

a3553.speaker: Emmanuel Birba, chief financial officer of Tulu Moye Geothermal Operations Plc
a3553.name: Emmanuel Birba
a3553.title: chief financial officer of Tulu Moye Geothermal Operations Plc
a3553.speech: Told his audience that dealing with Africa should not be seen as “a one-night stand.”

a3553.speaker: Emmanuel Birba, chief financial officer of Tulu Moye Geothermal Operations Plc
a3553.name: Emmanuel Birba
a3553.title: chief financial officer of Tulu Moye Geothermal Operations Plc
a3553.speech: Confident of his encounter with the prospective investors, has high hopes that by next year there will be a financial closing to secure close to 80pc of the 800 million dollars needed to finance the plant that will generate 150MW of power in its first phase.

a3553.speaker: A panelist at the Africa Investment Forum (unnamed)
a3553.name: A panelist at the Africa Investment Forum (unnamed)
a3553.speech: “You can’t dream big and invest small in Africa.”

a3553.speaker: Another panelist at the Africa Investment Forum (unnamed)
a3553.name: Another panelist at the Africa Investment Forum (unnamed)
a3553.speech: “If you aren’t in Africa, you aren’t in business.”

a3553.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, president of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3553.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3553.title: president of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3553.speech: “Africa is bankable. It’s impatient for development. It’s like a bride.”

a3553.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, president of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3553.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3553.title: president of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3553.speech: “Infrastructure should not be the preserve of governments. The Bank [AfDB] promotes the public-private partnership model,” Adesina cautioned leaders in attendance.

a3553.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, president of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3553.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a3553.title: president of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3553.speech: Echoed the views of the Forum, which is not a political but an investment platform, whereby a lot of preparation is required.

a3553.speaker: Neven Mimica, outgoing EU Commissioner for International Cooperation & Development
a3553.name: Neven Mimica
a3553.title: outgoing EU Commissioner for International Cooperation & Development
a3553.speech: Said Africa should not be a place for “a billion dollars in development assistance” but a market for “trillions of dollars in investment” ; “It’s an exciting time for Africa. We have to do more and faster.”

a3553.speaker: Ini J. Urua (PhD), senior vice president of the African Finance Corporation (AFC)
a3553.name: Ini J. Urua (PhD)
a3553.title: senior vice president of the African Finance Corporation (AFC)
a3553.speech: Said public-private partnership needs to be structured very well: “Yes, it does pay. We finance infrastructure, and we haven’t lost money.”

a3553.speaker: Sanjeev Gupta, executive director at the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC)
a3553.name: Sanjeev Gupta
a3553.title: executive director at the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC)
a3553.speech: Said the Forum represents “aggressiveness, adaptability and activeness.”

a3553.speaker: Mebarek, an investor from Egypt
a3553.name: Mebarek
a3553.title: an investor from Egypt
a3553.speech: Told an enthusiastic crowd that making deals at the Forum requires “discipline, process and rigor.”

a3667.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a3667.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a3667.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a3667.speech: In his welcome message, emphasized the geostrategic importance of the country: "Djibouti is a small country in size, but a country with immense strategic potential," ; "More than 90% of the foreign trade of Ethiopia, a neighboring country of more than 120 million inhabitants, transits through our ports," ; described the digital sector as "booming, with projects in cybersecurity, data centers and regional connectivity" ; said that to build a more diversified, inclusive and sustainable economy, Djibouti is counting on industrialization, "a strong private sector and better integration into global value chains" ; urged investors to seize the many opportunities on offer, particularly in logistics, agro-industry, renewable energies, tourism and vocational training, and committed to supporting potential investors with information, networking, administrative facilitation and advocacy ; "Our ambition is clear: to make Djibouti a bridge between continents, a competitive services center, and a reliable partner for all those who, like you, believe in the virtues of win-win trade and responsible investment."

a3667.speaker: Mohamed Ibrahim Ismail, President of the Minnesota Institute of Horn of Africa Studies and head of the American delegation
a3667.name: Mohamed Ibrahim Ismail
a3667.title: President of the Minnesota Institute of Horn of Africa Studies and head of the American delegation
a3667.speech: Did not hide his mission's desire to build lasting partnerships based on innovation and shared growth ; insisted on the importance of the infrastructures visited the day before - free zones, ports, technology centers - which embody Djibouti's ambitious vision for its future and that of the entire region ; expressed the willingness of members of the East African diaspora and American companies to participate actively in this dynamic, bringing not only their economic expertise but also their commitment, particularly in the commercial field but also in sectors beneficial to the economy, to the communities of both countries and to future generations.

a3667.speaker: Christopher Snipes, Charge d'affaires of the United States Embassy in Djibouti
a3667.name: Christopher Snipes
a3667.title: Charge d'affaires of the United States Embassy in Djibouti
a3667.speech: Recalled the multidimensional character of the partnership between Djibouti and Washington since 1977 and in particular its evolution in matters of security and military cooperation: "Collaborating with Djibouti to promote regional security will always remain one of our absolute priorities. Djibouti hosts the only American military base in Africa and our objective is to ensure that the United States and Djibouti continue to work together to promote peace and stability in the Horn of Africa."

a3667.speaker: Christopher Snipes, Charge d'affaires of the United States Embassy in Djibouti
a3667.name: Christopher Snipes
a3667.title: Charge d'affaires of the United States Embassy in Djibouti
a3667.speech: "This objective has long been at the heart of our strategy, and the embassy is now placing greater emphasis on the growth of American exports, support for American companies and the promotion of the private sector," ; encouraged American companies to consider Djibouti not only as a promising market, but also as a strategic gateway to the whole region ; expressed the hope that this trade mission would be only a starting point toward lasting and prosperous cooperation between the two countries.

a3667.speaker: Mohamed Warsama Dirieh, Djiboutian Minister of Commerce and Tourism
a3667.name: Mohamed Warsama Dirieh
a3667.title: Djiboutian Minister of Commerce and Tourism
a3667.speech: Welcomed the presence of an important delegation of American businessmen and businesswomen, which he considers a strong sign of growing interest in Djibouti as a strategic hub and regional investment platform ; mentioned the country's major assets, notably its exceptional geographical position, its world-class port infrastructure, its digital connectivity and its political stability, and recalled the numerous reforms undertaken by the government to improve the business environment and stimulate foreign investment ; emphasized the efforts made by Djibouti to take full advantage of AGOA and to strengthen trade with the United States ; reaffirmed Djibouti's commitment to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), an essential lever for developing regional value chains and attracting public-private partnerships ; committed to supporting investors and to making this forum a springboard for a renewed and ambitious economic partnership between the United States and Djibouti.

a3667.speaker: Executives of the National Tourism Agency (ANT), the Real Estate and Land Development Company (SIAF), the National Investment Promotion Agency (ANPI) and the Arreh & Deil firm
a3667.name: Executives of the National Tourism Agency (ANT)
a3667.title: the Real Estate and Land Development Company (SIAF), the National Investment Promotion Agency (ANPI) and the Arreh & Deil firm
a3667.speech: Took turns presenting the tourism potential, the real estate and investment opportunities as well as taxation in Djibouti.

a3738.speaker: World Bank
a3738.name: World Bank
a3738.speech: According to the World Bank, annual revenues from Malawi's mining sector are projected to hit US$3 billion by 2034, with mining contributing 12% of the country's GDP by 2027.

a3738.speaker: Feasibility study on the Kasiya Rutile-Graphite Project
a3738.name: Feasibility study on the Kasiya Rutile-Graphite Project
a3738.speech: A recent feasibility study estimated the project's revenue potential at US$16.4 billion, while US$665 million has been allocated for development.

a3833.speaker: Patricia Obozuwa, Vice President: Public Affairs, Communication, and Sustainability, Coca-Cola Africa
a3833.name: Patricia Obozuwa
a3833.title: Vice President: Public Affairs, Communication, and Sustainability, Coca-Cola Africa
a3833.speech: “[On] this International Women’s Day, we celebrate surpassing our goal to reach 5 million women, but we know that there is still work to be done” ; “Women entrepreneurs continue to face major hurdles hindering their successes, and we acknowledge that our work must therefore continue, particularly given the significant socio-economic disruption created by the pandemic in so many communities around the world”.

a3833.speaker: Patricia Obozuwa, Vice President: Public Affairs, Communication, and Sustainability, Coca-Cola Africa
a3833.name: Patricia Obozuwa
a3833.title: Vice President: Public Affairs, Communication, and Sustainability, Coca-Cola Africa
a3833.speech: “By investing in women’s economic empowerment over the past decade, we have created shared value in hopes of a better-shared future, enabling improved livelihoods for women, their families and their communities, while inclusively expanding our business” ; “We are proud about the ripple effects that these programs have had on the millions of lives we have touched and will continue to have over the years to come.”

a3833.speaker: Harvard Kennedy School Corporate Social Responsibility Initiative (study)
a3833.name: Harvard Kennedy School Corporate Social Responsibility Initiative (study)
a3833.speech: Found that through the UN Women partnership program the entrepreneurs increased their revenues by 40% on average and increased their confidence and leadership abilities within their communities.

a3833.speaker: Numerous studies from the United Nations and academic institutions
a3833.name: Numerous studies from the United Nations and academic institutions
a3833.speech: Have repeatedly proven that investment in women spurs economic growth and promotes sustainable development.

a3833.speaker: The Coca-Cola Company
a3833.name: The Coca-Cola Company
a3833.speech: This International Women’s Month, the Coca-Cola Company and its partners say they are proud to celebrate exceeding their 5by20 goal by enabling the economic empowerment of more than 6 million women around the world, about 34% (just over 2 million) of whom live and do business in Africa ; states that it is a global organisation but a local business, deeply rooted in the local communities it serves, and that it thrives as communities prosper.

a3939.speaker: Oxfam in Malawi
a3939.name: Oxfam in Malawi
a3939.speech: Has urged the Malawi Government to expand its social protection programmes to shield households from economic depression characterised by a rise in prices of maize and other basic commodities.

a3939.speaker: Lingalireni Mihowa, Oxfam in Malawi Country Director
a3939.name: Lingalireni Mihowa
a3939.title: Oxfam in Malawi Country Director
a3939.speech: Noted that many households in the country are in critical need of food as prices of maize and other basic commodities have gone up. Said Mihowa: “We would like to urge government to continue with social protection programmes, expand them where possible and make sure that there is more support that can come because the most critical need at household level is that of food.”

a3939.speaker: Martin Goche, Chikwawa District Council chairperson
a3939.name: Martin Goche
a3939.title: Chikwawa District Council chairperson
a3939.speech: Said the cash transfer will reduce the suffering of the households affected by hunger. “My appeal is that next time you will reach out to more people because there are many people here who have been affected by hunger.”

a3939.speaker: Esnart Kamonjola, 42-year-old beneficiary
a3939.name: Esnart Kamonjola
a3939.title: 42-year-old beneficiary
a3939.speech: Said her family of six had been struggling to get food and sometimes relied on tubers to survive. “Now we will use this money to buy a bag of maize.”

a3939.speaker: Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee report
a3939.name: Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee report
a3939.speech: Revealed last year that 5.7 million people would face hunger between October 2024 and March 2025.

a3960.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (statement to Eye Radio)
a3960.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (statement to Eye Radio)
a3960.speech: Said the funding will target communities in six high-risk counties, including Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Ayod, and Akobo in Jonglei State, and Panyikang and Fashoda in Upper Nile State, and that these areas have been severely affected by overlapping crises, leaving families in critical need of immediate humanitarian support ; said that since the escalation of conflict in Upper Nile State in March, more than 130,000 people have been displaced, including thousands who have reportedly crossed into Ethiopia, and that the ongoing rainy season is expected to bring heavy flooding to areas already affected in previous years.

a3960.speaker: Anita Kiki Gbeho, Humanitarian Coordinator for South Sudan
a3960.name: Anita Kiki Gbeho
a3960.title: Humanitarian Coordinator for South Sudan
a3960.speech: Said the funding will contribute to mitigating the dire situation: "This timely and much-needed CERF funding will contribute towards mitigating acute vulnerabilities and protection risks through coordinated interventions led by United Nations agencies and their partners in South Sudan" ; "The allocation must also catalyze to mobilize support for the millions more in need across the country." ; "CERF funding will help ensure they receive food, cash assistance, seeds, tools, fishing kits, shelter, non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene supplies, as well as health, nutrition, and protection services. They will also need continued support to restore their livelihoods and rebuild their lives."

a4069.speaker: United States Geological Survey (USGS)
a4069.name: United States Geological Survey (USGS)
a4069.speech: Reported the 8.8 magnitude quake hit 136 kilometers (84 miles) east of the coastal city of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky.

a4069.speaker: Japan's meteorological agency
a4069.name: Japan's meteorological agency
a4069.speech: Issued a tsunami advisory for much of its east coast, cautioning residents about potential waves up to 3 meters (9.8 feet) high.

a4069.speaker: Ecuador's Secretariat for Risk Management
a4069.name: Ecuador's Secretariat for Risk Management
a4069.speech: Confirmed a "tsunami warning has been established for the Insular Region [Galapagos], which indicates the immediate suspension of maritime activities, as well as preventive evacuations."

a4069.speaker: Al Jazeera
a4069.name: Al Jazeera
a4069.speech: Cited as the source reporting that Ecuadoran officials have ordered preventive evacuations from beaches, docks, and low-lying areas in the Galapagos Islands.

a4152.speaker: Alexandre Monteiro, Minister of Industry, Trade and Energy of Cabo Verde
a4152.name: Alexandre Monteiro
a4152.title: Minister of Industry, Trade and Energy of Cabo Verde
a4152.speech: Said the project represents an “impact that takes on an even more significant dimension when analysed in the context of the energy system of the island of Santiago. The combination of this plant with the other 10 MW plant already under way and with the expansion of the wind farm will allow renewable production capacity to be tripled, reaching about 42 MW.” ; Went on to say that, for the first time, the island of Santiago will have a production capacity higher than peak consumption, which is around 40 MW ; Said the new plant will have an estimated annual output of around 21 GWh, allowing savings of 5,125 tonnes of fuel per year and avoiding the emission of approximately 18,750 tonnes of CO2.

a4374.speaker: U.S. State Department
a4374.name: U.S. State Department
a4374.speech: Maintains its firm position against the terrorist activities of Boko Haram while ensuring rigorous control of the aid provided to the region; the United States on Wednesday reaffirmed their “condemnation of the violence and blatant disregard for human life” perpetrated by Boko Haram and other terrorist groups operating in Nigeria and the region.

a4374.speaker: Washington (U.S. government)
a4374.name: Washington (U.S. government)
a4374.speech: Stresses that it has put in place “comprehensive monitoring and evaluation systems” to guarantee that American aid effectively reaches its intended recipients.

a4374.speaker: U.S. State Department
a4374.name: U.S. State Department
a4374.speech: Also recalled its continued collaboration with Nigeria and its regional partners in the fight against terrorism, underlining the importance of a coordinated approach in the face of this persistent threat in West Africa.

a4504.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a4504.name: Wang Yi
a4504.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a4504.speech: Told Sri Lankan government officials that China has a blueprint for a development forum for Indian Ocean countries because they share "similar experiences and common needs"; he hinted at a new economic network for nations that share the waterway during his visit to Sri Lanka, echoing the economic message he had pressed home in the Comoros and Maldives.

a4504.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a4504.name: Wang Yi
a4504.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a4504.speech: In the Maldives, played up the significance of the 2-km Sinamale Bridge BRI project and pledged $63 million in new grants for infrastructure projects, which would include funds to cover the maintenance of the bridge ; made it clear that Beijing would not let its ties with Colombo be derailed over local anti-China sentiment.

a4504.speaker: Veteran South Asian diplomat (anonymous)
a4504.name: Veteran South Asian diplomat (anonymous)
a4504.speech: "Wang's visits to the Maldives and Sri Lanka were more strategic, to reinforce China's BRI diplomacy in the Indian Ocean, than bilateral diplomacy," one veteran diplomat told Nikkei Asia. "It is also showing that China will stick to its soft-power economic approach to stand apart from the conventional arms-and-containment approach of its geopolitical rivals."

a4504.speaker: Geopolitical analysts
a4504.name: Geopolitical analysts
a4504.speech: Say Wang's island-hopping conveys a message to India that Beijing is determined to secure beachheads in its backyard.

a4504.speaker: Nilanthi Samaranayake, director of strategy and policy analysis at the Washington think tank CNA
a4504.name: Nilanthi Samaranayake
a4504.title: director of strategy and policy analysis at the Washington think tank CNA
a4504.speech: Said Wang's tour "reinforces the importance of small states in the Indian Ocean for attention by major powers."

a4504.speaker: Nilanthi Samaranayake, director of strategy and policy analysis at the Washington think tank CNA
a4504.name: Nilanthi Samaranayake
a4504.title: director of strategy and policy analysis at the Washington think tank CNA
a4504.speech: Said an Indian vessel was in the Comoros to "provide ship repair assistance to the country's coast guard"; "It underscores India's continued engagement with Comoros, which has included delivery of rice and medical assistance by the Indian Navy in the past two years."

a4504.speaker: George Cooke, former Sri Lankan diplomat
a4504.name: George Cooke
a4504.title: former Sri Lankan diplomat
a4504.speech: "Even though Sri Lanka-China ties have gone through rocky moments last year, the Chinese know that they can wait" ; "Chinese are interested in the location, Sri Lanka's geography, and are pursuing smart diplomacy to avoid creating gaps for others to exploit."

a4541.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a4541.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4541.title: South African President
a4541.speech: Defended his land reform policy against Trump's attack, saying the government had not confiscated any land and that he looked forward to engaging with Trump to foster a better understanding over a policy he said ensures equitable public access to land ; said U.S. funding accounted for 17% of South Africa's HIV/AIDS programme but was not significant in other areas.

a4541.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a4541.name: Donald Trump
a4541.title: U.S. President
a4541.speech: Said on Sunday, without citing evidence, that “South Africa is confiscating land” and “certain classes of people” were being treated “very badly”, adding that he would cut off funding to the country in response.

a4541.speaker: Elon Musk, South African-born billionaire backer of Trump
a4541.name: Elon Musk
a4541.title: South African-born billionaire backer of Trump
a4541.speech: Said in a post on X the country had “openly racist ownership laws”, suggesting white people were the victims.

a4541.speaker: African National Congress (ANC)
a4541.name: African National Congress (ANC)
a4541.speech: Accused Trump of amplifying misinformation propagated by AfriForum, a right-wing lobby group; said Trump's attack was “a direct result of the lobby group's ongoing efforts to mislead the global community and protect apartheid-era land ownership”.

a4541.speaker: Kallie Kriel, AfriForum CEO
a4541.name: Kallie Kriel
a4541.title: AfriForum CEO
a4541.speech: Said his group would ask the U.S. government “to directly punish senior ANC leaders and not the people of South Africa” over land reform.

a4541.speaker: AfriForum spokesperson
a4541.name: AfriForum spokesperson
a4541.speech: Confirmed the group had lobbied in the United States.

a4541.speaker: Democratic Alliance (DA)
a4541.name: Democratic Alliance (DA)
a4541.speech: Said it wanted the land reform law to be amended to address certain flaws, but corrected Trump on the specifics: “It is not true that the Act allows land to be seized by the state arbitrarily, and it does require fair compensation for legitimate expropriations.”

a4541.speaker: Gwede Mantashe, South African Mining Minister (ANC)
a4541.name: Gwede Mantashe
a4541.title: South African Mining Minister (ANC)
a4541.speech: Said African countries should “withhold minerals” from the United States in response to any aid cut.

a4541.speaker: Vincent Magwenya, Ramaphosa's spokesperson
a4541.name: Vincent Magwenya
a4541.title: Ramaphosa's spokesperson
a4541.speech: Told Reuters those words should be “taken in jest” and the government was not seriously advocating such a policy.

a4541.speaker: Economists
a4541.name: Economists
a4541.speech: Said any U.S. measures against South Africa could hurt the economy at a time when the U.S./Africa AGOA trade deal is due for renewal and Ramaphosa has been struggling to boost growth and attract investors.

a4541.speaker: Charles Robertson, emerging markets specialist at FIM Partners
a4541.name: Charles Robertson
a4541.title: emerging markets specialist at FIM Partners
a4541.speech: “Do you want to set up a factory in a country where today, Trump's cutting off all aid? Maybe tomorrow, he's ripping up AGOA and maybe on Wednesday, he's adding 25% tariffs because they're too close to China”.

a4541.speaker: David Omojomolo, economist at Capital Economics (research)
a4541.name: David Omojomolo
a4541.title: economist at Capital Economics (research)
a4541.speech: Research showed South African exports to the U.S. through AGOA represented 1% of GDP in 2023, of which about half was transportation equipment; he said 56% of exports from South Africa's automotive sector were AGOA-eligible.

a4541.speaker: Parks Tau, South African Trade Minister
a4541.name: Parks Tau
a4541.title: South African Trade Minister
a4541.speech: Said the government would engage with the U.S. administration and both parties represented in Congress on the continuation of AGOA, which expires this year. “We are optimistic that we will remain part of AGOA,” he told Reuters on the sidelines of an African mining conference in Cape Town.

a4557.speaker: Robert Scott, interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.name: Robert Scott
a4557.title: interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.speech: Confirmed that relations between the two countries are in excellent shape: “Bilateral relations between the United States and Benin are very much strengthened. We made this visit with the aim of supporting Benin in its relations with the USA.”

a4557.speaker: Robert Scott, interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.name: Robert Scott
a4557.title: interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.speech: Announced works for the production and distribution of solar and hydroelectric power throughout Benin, with particular attention to Cotonou and Porto-Novo, under the second Millennium Challenge Account compact (MCA II), complementing the first compact focused on transport and the Autonomous Port of Cotonou ; “Africa is at the heart of US development programmes. I met the officials of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) and the people who handle the implementation of the MCA” ; assured that financing for this American programme is already available and that an update on its progress will be given to the population in the coming days ; said a Solar Fair will be organised next September in the United States, allowing the Beninese delegation and others “to discover the new off-grid energy system” with a view to testing it in their countries.

a4557.speaker: Robert Scott, interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.name: Robert Scott
a4557.title: interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.speech: Explained that he explored possibilities of collaboration between members of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB) and Beninese entrepreneurs with those of the USA, which will make it possible to develop relations in the trade sector and business opportunities between the two countries.

a4557.speaker: Robert Scott, interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.name: Robert Scott
a4557.title: interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.speech: Said he had discussed with the Beninese authorities the need for Benin to combat human trafficking, and hopes the relevant law will quickly be passed by the National Assembly so as to make progress in this area.

a4557.speaker: Robert Scott, interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.name: Robert Scott
a4557.title: interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.speech: Said that visiting the maritime operations centre will make it possible to better control Benin's coasts, trafficking, operations at sea and all illicit activities; announced a large-scale sub-regional operation next March aimed at ensuring the protection of the coasts; and gave reassurance that Benin is not threatened by maritime insecurity.

a4557.speaker: Robert Scott, interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.name: Robert Scott
a4557.title: interim US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs
a4557.speech: Said his visit to the Central Purchasing Agency for Essential Medicines (CAME) fell within the framework of the programme led by USAID and the President's Malaria Initiative in Benin.

a4778.speaker: “Nkosi” (pseudonym), gay male sex worker (voicemail to Bhekisisa)
a4778.name: “Nkosi” (pseudonym)
a4778.title: gay male sex worker (voicemail to Bhekisisa)
a4778.speech: “Hello, sis. How are you? I hope you're fine. I mean, I'm not.” ; “You know, I'm a gay guy. I have sex with other men, without wearing condoms now, because when I try to fetch them from my local clinic, I'm told I get judged and told I want too many. You know what's happening in our industry.”

a4778.speaker: World Health Organisation
a4778.name: World Health Organisation
a4778.speech: Says gay and bisexual men like Nkosi's chance of contracting HIV through sex is 26 [times] higher than that of the general population.

a4778.speaker: Research cited on treatment of key populations
a4778.name: Research cited on treatment of key populations
a4778.speech: People like Nkosi, research shows, are often treated badly by health workers at state clinics, making them wary of returning.

a4778.speaker: “Nkosi” (pseudonym), gay male sex worker
a4778.name: “Nkosi” (pseudonym)
a4778.title: gay male sex worker
a4778.speech: “So, sometimes I don't have PrEP. A partner can tell me he is on PrEP, but I don't trust that. Because where is he getting PrEP? Where am I going to get it? The black market? I don't know if it is even the real thing. Is it a counterfeit? Lube? That's another thing — you use everything, anything, as long as it's got jelly in it. The last time I did that I had an itchy penis for a week.”

a4778.speaker: “Nkosi” (pseudonym), gay male sex worker
a4778.name: “Nkosi” (pseudonym)
a4778.title: gay male sex worker
a4778.speech: Calls the domino effect of the Trump administration's decision to pull funding “the Donald disease because it is being caused by this guy, one man” ; “It's like crossing the freeway every day the way we're living now. One day, I know I'm gonna die.”

a4778.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister (press conference in May)
a4778.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a4778.title: South African Health Minister (press conference in May)
a4778.speech: Called a press conference in May to present his “18 facts” about the crisis, eight of those points being about what government is doing to make sure the patients from those specialised clinics — over 63 300 patients — were taken care of and that their files have been transferred to the nearest government facility.

a4778.speaker: UNAids
a4778.name: UNAids
a4778.speech: Says more than half of all new infections in 2022, around the world, came from key populations — and infections don't stay within those groups.

a4778.speaker: Francois Venter, head of the health research organisation Ezintsha at Wits University
a4778.name: Francois Venter
a4778.title: head of the health research organisation Ezintsha at Wits University
a4778.speech: “Even the most self-interested people should be heavily invested in treatment and prevention of these populations” ; “There's no clean, magical division between key populations and general populations. It's a Venn diagram of married men sleeping with sex workers, of drug-using populations interacting with your ostensibly innocent kids, gay men with your straight-presenting son, all needing HIV prevention and treatment programmes.”

a4778.speaker: Studies on oral PrEP adherence
a4778.name: Studies on oral PrEP adherence
a4778.speech: Studies show that getting people to use the anti-HIV pill, also called oral PrEP, each day, has been a struggle — and those who do use it often don't use it each day; the less often it's used, the less well it works.

a4778.speaker: Researchers (estimates on South African HIV treatment)
a4778.name: Researchers (estimates on South African HIV treatment)
a4778.speech: Researchers estimate that of South Africa's 8 million people with HIV, 1.1 million people who have been diagnosed with HIV are not on treatment.

a4778.speaker: Modelling studies
a4778.name: Modelling studies
a4778.speech: Modelling studies show there's a high chance that we see up to 300 000 extra HIV infections over the next four years and a 38% increase in Aids deaths if the lost health workers are not replaced.

a4778.speaker: Researchers who surveyed over 9 000 people in key populations
a4778.name: Researchers who surveyed over 9 000 people in key populations
a4778.speech: Found that less than half, and in some cases not even a quarter, said they were treated well; about one in five said they were blocked from getting services.

a4778.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a4778.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a4778.title: South African Health Minister
a4778.speech: Says he's trying to fix stigma and discrimination in public clinics by now training 1 012 clinicians and 2 377 non-clinician workers at government facilities in non-discriminatory healthcare.

a4778.speaker: Female sex worker (anonymous, voice note)
a4778.name: Female sex worker (anonymous
a4778.title: voice note)
a4778.speech: “Yoh, life is very hard. Since all this happened, life has been very, very hard.” ; “I have tried to go to the public clinic for my medication. But as sex workers, we are not being helped. We are scared to go to the government clinic to treat sexually transmitted infections because we are seen as dirty people who go and sleep around. We even struggle to get condoms. We are now forced to do business without protection because it is only our source of income and it's the way that we put food on the table. My worry now is that I am pregnant and my child is going to be infected because I'm not taking my ARVs, and I have defaulted for two months now.”

a4778.speaker: Transgender woman (anonymous, voice note)
a4778.name: Transgender woman (anonymous
a4778.title: voice note)
a4778.speech: “I'm a transgender woman. My pronouns are she.” ; “When the clinic closed, I was about to run out of medication so I went to the government clinic in my area... The lady told me that they can't help me and I need to bring the transfer letter. I told her that the clinic is closed so I don't have the transfer letter. I asked to speak to the manager and the manager also refused to help me. The manager! How can she let someone who is HIV-positive go home without medication? I had to call one of my friends and she gave me one container. If you're not taking your medication consistently, you're going to get sick, you're gonna die. And the future? The future is dark.”

a4778.speaker: Migrant farm worker (anonymous, voice note)
a4778.name: Migrant farm worker (anonymous
a4778.title: voice note)
a4778.speech: “When we were told that the clinic was closed, I was actually in another town trying to get a seasonal job on the farms. But when I went to the nearest clinic, I was told that I needed to get a transfer letter. So I ended up sharing medication with friends. But then their medication also ran out... Now we went to the clinic and spent the whole day there because we had to follow the queues... I went to the government clinic and asked to get at least three months' supply. But the clinic said no because it was my first initiation so I had to come back. So I went back to the farm to see if I could still have my job. I found that I was no longer employed because they had to take up someone else. What am I going to do? If I go to the clinic, I stand a chance of losing my job. If I stay at my job, I am at risk of getting sick.”

a4778.speaker: Transwoman (anonymous, voice note)
a4778.name: Transwoman (anonymous
a4778.title: voice note)
a4778.speech: “Accessing treatment is difficult because of the long queues. Even that security guard keeps on telling me to go away when I ask for lubricants and he tells me every time there's no lubricants. We need the trans clinic back. I need to speak to somebody, a psychologist. On Tuesdays we had our psychologist come in, and the doctor. But now I don't have the funds to go and see even a psychologist. It is bad. It is super bad. I don't know when I last took my meds. Another friend of mine just decided, oh, okay, since the clinic is closed and I no longer have medication, I'll just stay home and die.”

a4817.speaker: Monitngn / MonitNG, civic technology platform
a4817.name: Monitngn / MonitNG
a4817.title: civic technology platform
a4817.speech: A recent visit to the health post by the civic technology platform revealed shocking conditions — cracked and crumbling walls, a leaking roof, and no electricity to power even basic medical equipment; the centre also lacks beds, essential drugs, trained staff, and a perimeter fence, exposing both patients and health workers to danger.

a4817.speaker: A resident of Sakace Ward (anonymous)
a4817.name: A resident of Sakace Ward (anonymous)
a4817.speech: “The situation is so dire that, according to a resident, snakes and other reptiles frequently crawl into the wards. In some instances, humans and animals have found themselves sharing the same unsafe space.”

a4817.speaker: Monitngn / MonitNG, civic technology platform
a4817.name: Monitngn / MonitNG
a4817.title: civic technology platform
a4817.speech: “Because of the region's insecurity, some communities no longer have access to the center, putting already vulnerable populations at even greater risk.” ; “What’s most troubling is that this is happening despite years of government promises and several donor-funded health interventions. Partners such as USAID, eHealth Africa, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, the Aliko Dangote Foundation, the Sultan Foundation for Peace and Development, and MAP International have all supported healthcare improvements in Kebbi. Yet, Bakinturu Health Post remains untouched.”

a4817.speaker: Former Kebbi State government
a4817.name: Former Kebbi State government
a4817.speech: committed to revitalising primary healthcare across all political wards in the state.

a4817.speaker: Current Kebbi State administration
a4817.name: Current Kebbi State administration
a4817.speech: has spoken about prioritising health and even plans to increase health sector investments.

a4817.speaker: Monitngn / MonitNG, civic technology platform
a4817.name: Monitngn / MonitNG
a4817.title: civic technology platform
a4817.speech: “But words are not enough. We need visible, measurable change in the lives of people in rural communities. The residents of Sakace and surrounding villages deserve dignity, safety, and access to proper healthcare”; has called on Governor Nasir Idris to take urgent action to renovate and equip the health post, insisting that rural citizens deserve the same basic healthcare access as those in urban areas.

a4945.speaker: Russian Ambassador to Mozambique
a4945.name: Russian Ambassador to Mozambique
a4945.speech: Speaking in Maputo during a visit to the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique, made it known that his country has state-of-the-art heavy machinery that could change the scenario (for increasing bilateral trade beyond the current one hundred million US dollars).

a4945.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4945.name: Filipe Nyusi
a4945.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4945.speech: Says that we should not watch road accidents impassively and calmly ; says that with the collaboration of the Attorney General's Office and the Courts it is urgent to hold accountable all those who cause this misfortune, considered a public calamity. The Head of State was speaking on Thursday at the second National Symposium on Road Safety.

a4945.speaker: Health Sector (Mozambique)
a4945.name: Health Sector (Mozambique)
a4945.speech: Fears that the refusal of Nampula residents to accept indoor residual spraying may contribute to an increase in malaria cases.

a4945.speaker: Leopoldo da Costa, Deputy Minister of Health of Mozambique
a4945.name: Leopoldo da Costa
a4945.title: Deputy Minister of Health of Mozambique
a4945.speech: Said that the Ministry should grant more resources to the Jose Macamo General Hospital, with a view to improving care for citizens.

a4945.speaker: Study on the Education Sector in Mozambique (released in Maputo)
a4945.name: Study on the Education Sector in Mozambique (released in Maputo)
a4945.speech: Reveals the main problems that still affect the education sector in Mozambique, starting with the excessive absences of primary school teachers from classes; indicates a worrying teacher/student ratio, with one teacher ending up teaching eighty students, hence the difficulty of providing proper follow-up; according to the data, many primary schools have reactivated school councils and the school-community relationship has improved significantly, so much so that the community often helps build schools with local material or monetary contributions.

a4945.speaker: Government of Mozambique / Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, Prime Minister
a4945.name: Government of Mozambique / Carlos Agostinho do Rosario
a4945.title: Prime Minister
a4945.speech: Says it is not paying the public debt, because negotiations with creditors are underway regarding the process of the so-called hidden debts, in a statement during the session of deputies' questions to the government.

a4945.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a4945.name: Government of Mozambique
a4945.speech: Reiterates the existence of challenges in urban transport which it guarantees it will overcome; reiterates that infrastructure development is at the top of its governance priorities, with particular attention to projects extending the water supply network ; says the 2016/2017 agricultural campaign was a success, having surpassed the two previous ones, and guarantees it will stimulate actions in the agricultural sector to overcome the challenges that still prevail in marketing.

a4945.speaker: Participants of the II edition of the Macaneta beach festival
a4945.name: Participants of the II edition of the Macaneta beach festival
a4945.speech: Expressed the sentiment that the festival in Marracuene, Maputo province, reinforces national unity and contributes to the growth of Mozambican culture and tourism.

a5032.speaker: Guo Jiakun, spokesman for the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5032.name: Guo Jiakun
a5032.title: spokesman for the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5032.speech: Said at a press conference that “the China–Russia relationship maintains a healthy, stable and high-level development under the strategic guidance of the two heads of State”, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, and considered that bilateral exchanges have been deepening steadily in various fields ; added that during the visit Wang will hold talks with Lavrov to exchange views on the bilateral agenda, regional cooperation and international questions of common interest.

a5032.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a5032.name: Xi Jinping
a5032.title: President of China
a5032.speech: Has stressed on several occasions that maintaining robust relations with Russia is a “strategic choice” for Beijing.

a5156.speaker: Economic and Financial Crimes Court (EFCC), three-member bench (court ruling)
a5156.name: Economic and Financial Crimes Court (EFCC)
a5156.title: three-member bench (court ruling)
a5156.speech: Has ordered the forfeiture of former Ministry of Defence Permanent Secretary Stardy Mwale’s US$2.5 million farm to the State because the asset is a proceed of crime, and condemned Mr Mwale and three other interested parties in the case to costs. The court ruled that based on its detailed analysis, it was of the well-considered view that the applicant, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), had established on the balance of probabilities that the farm is tainted.

a5156.speaker: Judge Susan Wanjelani, reading the judgment on behalf of judges Ian Mabbolobbolo and Vincent Siloka
a5156.name: Judge Susan Wanjelani
a5156.title: reading the judgment on behalf of judges Ian Mabbolobbolo and Vincent Siloka
a5156.speech: “The property is liable to forfeiture as envisaged under the Forfeiture of Proceeds of Crime Act No. 19 of 2010.” ; “Accordingly, we order that the Simonga farm be forfeited to the State.”

a5446.speaker: Michael Biswick Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a5446.name: Michael Biswick Usi
a5446.title: Vice President of Malawi
a5446.speech: Made a compelling case for reimagining global financing systems—boldly urging international partners to move from rhetoric to action, and from pledges to tangible support for nations like Malawi; his addresses centered on a recurring message: Malawi, and many nations like it, are disproportionately affected by global shocks, yet continue to be sidelined in global financial structures. He called for a radical shift that would see vulnerability to shocks—like climate change and economic instability—used as a basis for access to concessional financing ; “It's no longer enough to name the challenges. The time has come to deliver real, practical solutions.” ; urged reforms in the mandates of multilateral development banks, credit rating systems, and fair access to liquidity for developing nations, arguing for debt relief and restructuring for nations overwhelmed by repayment burdens, highly concessional loans tailored to LDC realities, enhanced representation of developing countries in financial decision-making spaces, and increased transparency in climate financing mechanisms.

a5446.speaker: Michael Biswick Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a5446.name: Michael Biswick Usi
a5446.title: Vice President of Malawi
a5446.speech: At a high-level roundtable co-hosted by the Gates Foundation and DEVEX, called for targeted financing in health and human capital development: “No development will be sustainable if our people are sick and dying young. Human capital is the bedrock of progress.” He cited the long-standing success of Malawi's HIV programmes, backed by the Global Fund, as evidence that smart, targeted investments in health can yield national dividends.

a5446.speaker: Michael Biswick Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a5446.name: Michael Biswick Usi
a5446.title: Vice President of Malawi
a5446.speech: Strongly condemned the endless cycles of “talk-shop” COP meetings that, in his words, leave Malawi “with no real benefit despite bearing the brunt of climate shocks” ; “Fancy global statements are not always useful. We need to diagnose our problems and act with precision. The people in the Global South need solutions—not slogans.”

a5446.speaker: EU officials present at the conference
a5446.name: EU officials present at the conference
a5446.speech: According to EU officials present at the conference, Usi's candour “cut through the diplomatic fog” that usually clouds such forums.

a5446.speaker: An EU Commissioner (unnamed)
a5446.name: An EU Commissioner (unnamed)
a5446.speech: Praised Usi for “telling it like it is.”

a5446.speaker: Officials from Norway, Iceland and Luxembourg
a5446.name: Officials from Norway
a5446.title: Iceland and Luxembourg
a5446.speech: In bilateral meetings, reaffirmed support in key sectors like health, education and governance.

a5446.speaker: Luxembourg
a5446.name: Luxembourg
a5446.speech: Luxembourg, which previously channelled aid through the EU, expressed interest in establishing direct cooperation with Malawi.

a5564.speaker: James Dorbor Jallah, Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority
a5564.name: James Dorbor Jallah
a5564.title: Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority
a5564.speech: "While paying taxes is a civic duty, the LRA acknowledges that taxes play a crucial role in supporting public sector investments and development across all spheres of government. Those who consistently meet their tax obligations deserve recognition and encouragement."

a5602.speaker: Quian Anuha, President of Antex Group
a5602.name: Quian Anuha
a5602.title: President of Antex Group
a5602.speech: Says they repeatedly reported the problem to government agencies with no avail; said that he told Abebe Abebayehu, who runs the Ethiopian Investment Commission, Lelise Neme, CEO of Industrial Park Development, the Mayor of Adama and Adama police station but no one responded ; "I never encountered this type of situation in other countries so we don't know how to solve the problem."

a5602.speaker: Quian Anuha, President of Antex Group
a5602.name: Quian Anuha
a5602.title: President of Antex Group
a5602.speech: "It is not only about the money, the nature of the machines by themselves requires a high amount of security because much damage has occurred to the company's property previously."

a5602.speaker: Quian Anuha, President of Antex Group
a5602.name: Quian Anuha
a5602.title: President of Antex Group
a5602.speech: Partially blames the Adama police officers for not doing their jobs ; "Unless there is protection for investors, this will be a big trouble for the economy and hurt the image of the country."

a5602.speaker: Adama police
a5602.name: Adama police
a5602.speech: Have told him that blocking the machines was not a criminal act or that they did not have a jurisdiction.

a5602.speaker: The youth blocking the containers
a5602.name: The youth blocking the containers
a5602.speech: Claim that they do not have jobs and need money; they told the manager of Antex that unemployment has forced them to do this action ; they are asking for a hefty sum of money before they are willing to leave and want to be paid per container and even single machines.

a5602.speaker: Ephrem Bekel, Operation Manager of Adama Industrial Park
a5602.name: Ephrem Bekel
a5602.title: Operation Manager of Adama Industrial Park
a5602.speech: "The problem occurred because of a misunderstanding between youth and the Adama City Administration. The City is holding discussions with the people blocking the containers to solve the problem."

a5602.speaker: Lelise Neme, CEO of Industrial Park Development
a5602.name: Lelise Neme
a5602.title: CEO of Industrial Park Development
a5602.speech: Said that she would ask the Ethiopian Investment Commission about the case, saying that she does not know about it.

a5602.speaker: Antex Group (the company)
a5602.name: Antex Group (the company)
a5602.speech: Refrained from disclosing how much damage they had suffered.

a5672.speaker: African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy (document)
a5672.name: African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy (document)
a5672.speech: “AI systems may perpetuate or amplify biases contained in datasets that they are trained on because, more often, data are not equitably sourced - data are usually sourced from developed countries and from non-diverse and inclusive developers’ teams” ; noted that the indirect needs of AI may also exacerbate existing issues like water scarcity (due to the use of water cooling systems), carbon dioxide emissions as well as potentially delivering a blow to “African values”.

a5672.speaker: African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy (document)
a5672.name: African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy (document)
a5672.speech: “AI’s impact on the global economy is impressive. According to PwC, AI automation has the potential to add US$15.7 trillion to the world economy by 2030 and double economic growth rates by 2035 via productivity gains and transformation of how the government and business operate. This is equivalent to a 14% gain in global gross domestic product [GDP].”

a5672.speaker: PwC (cited)
a5672.name: PwC (cited)
a5672.speech: According to PwC, AI automation has the potential to add US$15.7 trillion to the world economy by 2030 and double economic growth rates by 2035 via productivity gains and transformation of how the government and business operate, equivalent to a 14% gain in global GDP.

a5672.speaker: African Union (AU)
a5672.name: African Union (AU)
a5672.speech: Remains hopeful that growing internet use on the continent, from 20% in 2015 to 40% in 2023, may lay the foundation for the use of AI ; “Even though the benefits of AI remain high for the continent, recent developments indicate a growing concern about the AI divide between Africa and the rest of the world due to the lack of high-quality and large datasets, lack of high-performance computers and talent capabilities that are critical for AI development and use.”

a5672.speaker: African Union (AU)
a5672.name: African Union (AU)
a5672.speech: Is hopeful that a young population and the continuous emergence of digitalisation may aid Africans in capacitating themselves to not be left out of the AI revolution: “Africa’s nascent digitalisation process of its heritage and culture is making it less vulnerable to AI misuse and presents opportunities for the effective protection of its identity online. Africa’s demographic make-up, characterised by a youthful population that largely consists of digital natives, further accentuates this trajectory. The continent’s younger generation perceives AI as an opportunity to address the unique challenges intrinsic to the continent.”

a5672.speaker: African Union (AU)
a5672.name: African Union (AU)
a5672.speech: Has instructed member states to establish working legal frameworks to ensure the safety of Africans amid the dangers posed by AI, and called for continuous assessment of AI-related threats; it also recommended the establishing of an independent AI ethics board at regional level.

a5672.speaker: African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy (document)
a5672.name: African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy (document)
a5672.speech: Envisions that AI could have the biggest impact in addressing challenges related to agriculture and food security, health, education, environment and climate change: “There are already a number of small-scale use cases of AI in Africa, including tools for identifying and diagnosing crop diseases and pests, predicting the price of agricultural produce, providing expert advice and giving farmers access to financial services, so there is a need to document and share AI solutions in the sector.”

a5672.speaker: African Union (AU)
a5672.name: African Union (AU)
a5672.speech: Warned that over-reliance on AI may stifle the creativity of young African minds: “AI must also not threaten teachers’ rights and undermine learners’ thinking processes and creativity, which in turn negatively affect innovation. Africa is a young continent where innovation plays a central role in establishing an African-owned and African-driven solution.”

a5748.speaker: United States government
a5748.name: United States government
a5748.speech: "The United States strongly condemns the attack carried out by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) on the airport in Asmara, Eritrea, on November 14."

a5748.speaker: Francisco Madeira, Special Representative of the Chairperson of the African Union Commission (SRCC) for Somalia
a5748.name: Francisco Madeira
a5748.title: Special Representative of the Chairperson of the African Union Commission (SRCC) for Somalia
a5748.speech: Today congratulated the government and the people of Djibouti on the country's 43rd Independence anniversary.

a5748.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists
a5748.name: Committee to Protect Journalists
a5748.speech: Said today that authorities in Djibouti should stop harassing journalists working with the La Voix de Djibouti broadcaster, and ensure that the press can cover matters of public interest without intimidation.

a5748.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a5748.name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a5748.speech: Condemns the arrests of two Djiboutian journalists working for La Voix de Djibouti (LVD), their small Horn of African country's only independent media outlet, and calls for their unconditional release.

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: addressed the role of African states within the UN and called for concrete measures, notably the granting of at least one permanent seat on the UN Security Council to African countries ; advocated abolishing the unlimited veto right of the victorious countries of the Second World War by giving the UN General Assembly the power to override vetoes by a vote.

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: called for the lifting of the blockade of Cuba, the Island of Freedom, which contributed greatly to the destruction of the apartheid regime in Africa; criticised the bias of Western states on the question of illegal immigration: the West is ready to support Ukrainian refugees while regarding migrants from the South as pathological criminals.

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: underlined his commitment to the creation of an independent Palestinian state and described Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip as a crime: “The crimes committed in Gaza must stop!” (declared twice).

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: reminded the world of the use of African slavery, the colonial exploitation of Africa's natural resources over centuries and the theft of precious cultural objects by representatives of Western civilisation; declared that the question of reparations must be resolved unequivocally in favour of African countries.

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: recalled that, with the increase in military spending worldwide, humanitarian aid is being rapidly reduced; in 2025 its volume was cut by 40% compared with 2024, which constitutes a hard blow to any development initiative.

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: demanded the removal of mining concessions granted to foreign companies in developing countries, seen as a means of maintaining inequality and diverting national wealth.

a5807.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5807.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5807.title: President of Ghana
a5807.speech: underlined the need to guarantee gender equality, notably equality of opportunity in politics; according to Mahama, his country is a positive example, since with the election of Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang to the vice-presidency the representation of women in Ghanaian politics has reached a fundamentally new level.

a5807.speaker: Ghanaian opposition
a5807.name: Ghanaian opposition
a5807.speech: had already called on the government to abandon its acerbic rhetoric concerning the events in Gaza.

a6062.speaker: SMS published in The Namibian newspaper, 16 November 2021 (anonymous reader)
a6062.name: SMS published in The Namibian newspaper
a6062.title: 16 November 2021 (anonymous reader)
a6062.speech: It read: “To the ministry of education: Pupils should not be stopped from attending school because of their haircuts. Most principals force all pupils to have a particular haircut but the truth is haircut has no any effect on education”.

a6062.speaker: Executive Director, Ministry of Education (Namibia)
a6062.name: Executive Director
a6062.title: Ministry of Education (Namibia)
a6062.speech: sided with those who protested against the school practice, as quoted in the media in September 2021.

a6062.speaker: Martin Luther King Jnr
a6062.name: Martin Luther King Jnr
a6062.speech: “Ask not what your country can do for you, but what you can do for your country.”

a6102.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a6102.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a6102.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a6102.speech: Called for urgent reforms of the global financial system to unlock Africa's full potential, saying that with the reforms it is possible to build a financial architecture that benefits everyone: "Let us align capital with our development priorities and build a 21st-century financial architecture that benefits everyone," he stated in a speech at the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4) in Seville.

a6102.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission (per an African Union statement)
a6102.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a6102.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission (per an African Union statement)
a6102.speech: Stressed that business and private finance "are not simply complementary, but catalysts of inclusive growth, job creation and the green transition."

a6102.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a6102.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a6102.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a6102.speech: Noted that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which aims to create the world's largest single market for goods and services, represents a "radical change" for the continent, and argued for greater support for foreign direct investment; concluded: "Africa is young, resource-rich and ready."

a6228.speaker: Hespress (Moroccan news outlet)
a6228.name: Hespress (Moroccan news outlet)
a6228.speech: Reports that the United Kingdom considers the autonomy proposal presented by Morocco in 2007 to be the "most credible, viable and pragmatic" basis for a lasting solution to the dispute over the Sahara.

a6228.speaker: Joint communique signed in Rabat by David Lammy, British Secretary of State, and Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6228.name: Joint communique signed in Rabat by David Lammy
a6228.title: British Secretary of State, and Nasser Bourita, Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6228.speech: Sets out the British position on the Moroccan autonomy plan; London states that it is closely following the dynamic driven by King Mohammed VI and commits to supporting the process at the bilateral, regional and international levels.

a6228.speaker: Le360 (Moroccan news outlet)
a6228.name: Le360 (Moroccan news outlet)
a6228.speech: Reports that the Saham group is preparing to change the corporate name of its bank as part of a strategic repositioning, with an extraordinary general meeting scheduled for 24 June to ratify the transformation, without any change to capital or headquarters.

a6228.speaker: L'Economiste, relaying UN Tourism data
a6228.name: L'Economiste
a6228.title: relaying UN Tourism data
a6228.speech: Notes that more than 300 million tourists travelled internationally in the first quarter of 2025, an increase of 5% compared with 2024 and of 3% compared with 2019, before the pandemic.

a6228.speaker: Observalgerie (Algerian news outlet)
a6228.name: Observalgerie (Algerian news outlet)
a6228.speech: Reports that the authorities are launching the forest-fire campaign with a reinforced aerial capability - 12 water-bomber aircraft, six intervention helicopters and two reconnaissance aircraft - and that the Minister of the Interior is personally supervising the preparations.

a6228.speaker: TSA Algerie (Algerian news outlet)
a6228.name: TSA Algerie (Algerian news outlet)
a6228.speech: Returns to Algiers' reaction to the British recognition of the Moroccan autonomy plan, expressing its "regret" and marking its disapproval, in a context where London joins Madrid and Paris on this issue.

a6228.speaker: La Presse (Tunisian newspaper)
a6228.name: La Presse (Tunisian newspaper)
a6228.speech: Announces the forthcoming opening of an office of the IUCN Centre for Mediterranean Cooperation, dedicated to water management, biodiversity and sustainability.

a6228.speaker: Africa Manager (Tunisian news outlet)
a6228.name: Africa Manager (Tunisian news outlet)
a6228.speech: Mentions the strengthening of Tunisian-Iranian tourism ties through the launch of direct flights, seen as a vector of cultural and economic rapprochement.

a6228.speaker: Libya Observer
a6228.name: Libya Observer
a6228.speech: Indicates that Prime Minister Dbeibah calls for a responsible partnership with the municipalities to guarantee stability and the provision of public services, in a logic of territorial security and of ending impunity for armed groups.

a6228.speaker: Libyan Express
a6228.name: Libyan Express
a6228.speech: Reports that two commissions of inquiry have been set up by the Attorney General to examine alleged abuses committed in Tripoli by the security forces in the context of the recent unrest.

a6228.speaker: Egyptian national press agency
a6228.name: Egyptian national press agency
a6228.speech: Reports the joint efforts of Cairo and Doha, in coordination with the United States, to reach a 60-day truce in Gaza, as a prelude to a lasting ceasefire and the delivery of humanitarian aid.

a6228.speaker: Egypt Today
a6228.name: Egypt Today
a6228.speech: Reports that Sharm El Sheikh has become Egypt's first green city, joining the International Council for Local Environmental Initiatives (ICLEI) of sustainable cities, and that a digital platform, www.greensharm.org, has been launched to promote its ecological initiatives and inform tourists.

a6479.speaker: Enoch Banda, 44-year-old factory worker in Lilongwe’s Kanengo Industrial Area
a6479.name: Enoch Banda
a6479.title: 44-year-old factory worker in Lilongwe’s Kanengo Industrial Area
a6479.speech: “I used to feel proud. Now, I feel like I’m just working to stay broke.” ; “By the time I buy food, pay rent and get charcoal to cook, I’m already in debt.” ; “I can’t even afford a bottle of beer. And that’s the least of my worries.”

a6479.speaker: Mike, 29-year-old shop attendant in Bwalo la Njobvu
a6479.name: Mike
a6479.title: 29-year-old shop attendant in Bwalo la Njobvu
a6479.speech: “I don’t live anymore. I survive. Barely.”

a6479.speaker: Centre for Social Concern (CfSC)
a6479.name: Centre for Social Concern (CfSC)
